items.body:
Mika Vainio’s swansong Ø album is arguably his solo magnum opus: a deeply personalised set of sonic postcards limning a distant archipelago of discrete sonic isles, ultimately leading to one of his most precious pieces in curtain closer ‘Loputon’ - an ideal epitaph to a peerless and hugely inspirational oeuvre that's become a byword for richly expressive minimalism.

Eight years since the passing of Mika Vainio (1963-2017), the Finnish artist’s formidable yet beautiful spirit lives on in his music with final album ‘Sysivalo’, which was nearing completion before he left this mortal coil far too early. Named as a portmanteau of “sysi” (dark or sinister) and “valo” (light) it locates Vainio inhabiting space between dimensions with an all too profound grasp of metaphysical, musical dark matter, counterweighted with glimpses of the sublime. It sounds closest to our ears in scope and feel to his 2005 masterpiece ‘Kantamoinen’ - a sort of nostalgic reverie for his grandmother - and shares flashes of that LP’s tangibly melancholic pathos tempering and illuminating a sequence of typically ascetic, elemental soundscapes and psychoacoustic sorcery. 

In the short time we’ve spent in its wilds, it’s clear that the post mortem completion, by Rikke Lundgreen and Tommi Grönlund in accordance with Mika’s notes, makes for many welcome returns to its expanse of endless drones and aurora borealis light shows, riddled with pangs of disarmingly gorgeous melody and atmospheric levity. Mika’s knack for giving noise character is in none more gripping effect on the journey thru its 20 vignette-sized chapters, adding up to a mazy mosaic or map of channels and islets for armchair and headphone navigation, weaving from emotionally pregnant panoramic tundras to fragile music box melodies, pitch-bent guitar shimmers and the odd precision-deployed bass pulse.

A northerly breeze puts wind behind noumenal sails on the initial blast of ‘Etudes’, spanning bits of uncannily throaty resonances and harmonic blushes to thawed goth string motifs  and mouth-watering, cavernous bass tones of ‘Etude 5’ and ’Sylvannus.’ At its core ‘Katko’ yields ephemeral fragrances of his gran’s garden, as heard on ‘Kantamoinen’, and felt in the creaking keys of ‘Uusikuu’ or music box wist of ‘Anthem’, whereas the gravelly swill of ’T-Bahn’ is the set’s only beat-driven piece, perhaps his ode to longtime home Berlin, as hinted in the title. And ultimately the final trio of his barely-there title piece, the shine-eyed star-gazer ‘Ursa’ and ‘Loputon (Endless)’ quietly radiate hope in the negative nether; an apt metaphor for all Mika’s work. 'Etudes 4' even uncannily sounds like The Cure's 'If Only Tonight We Could Sleep?' stripped to its barest bones - the closest Mika probably ever came to some ice cold variant of shoegaze.
items._cn_summary: Mika Vainio 生前遗作《Sysivalo》以极简手法构建出深邃的声场空间，专辑名取芬兰语中"黑暗"与"光"的合成词，贯穿对立统一的哲学意味。全作由20个短小章节组成，涵盖从极简drone到冰晶般音乐盒旋律的广阔频谱，低频脉冲与高频弦乐碎片交替出现。后期由Rikke Lundgreen与Tommi Grönlund根据Vainio遗留笔记完成混音制作，既保留了潘诺拉马般的荒凉北国氛围，也注入了克制而敏锐的情感温度。与2005年《Kantamoinen》形成互文，后者是对祖母的记忆，此作则像写给虚空的情书。

items.body:
Oren Ambarchi's kraut-techno-free jazz magnum opus is back for its 10th anniversary -  an ambitious ensemble piece featuring an all-star list of players including Ricardo Villalobos, Keith Fullerton Whitman, Mark Fell, crys Cole, Will Guthrie, Arto Lindsay and Konrad Sprenger... Wooooo

You've got to admire Ambarchi's chutzpah here. 'Hubris' is an all you can eat buffet of his various musical cravings, a chance for his friends, influences and collaborators to flex a little and for Ambarchi to attempt to ride the groove like an experienced cowboy on an out-of-control bucking bronco. The first side is the biggest surprise, a dedication to Wang Chung's enduring, disco-influenced 'To Live and Die in L.A.' soundtrack that begins with ping-ponging guitar notes and Jim O'Rourke's synth blips, before elusive Berlin-based composer Konrad Sprenger (aka Joerg Hiller) drops in with some motorized guitar vamps. It's rhythmic gear that fits in with the Berlin school until Mark Fell appears in the final third with some typically fractured percussion.

On the flip, the groove loosens after a short guitar interlude. Ricardo Villalobos takes over with a suitably winding, minimal throb over live rhythms played by Joe Talia and Will Guthrie simultaneously as krautrock techno mutates into disco fusion. Keith Fullerton Whitman tries to nudge the track off the rails with his modular expositions, but the path is set - Arto Lindsay's axe is just the icing on the cake. By the end of the side, we're in full jazz-noise mode: everything's still pegged to Villalobos' central pulse, but that's the only element that's bolted down. 

Hard to believe it's 10 years already - we can't think of a better skeleton key to unlock the secrets behind Black Truffle's musical identity.
items._genre: krautrock / experimental techno / free jazz / improvisation
items._cn_summary: Oren Ambarchi 第十周年再版的鸿篇巨制，融合了克拉夫特摇滚的循环节奏、极简电子的律动骨架与自由爵士的即兴张力。专辑分两面展开：A 面以吉他弹跳音符与 Jim O'Rourke 的合成器碎片开场，向 Wang Chung 的八十年代迪斯科配乐致敬，Konrad Sprenger 的机械化吉他连复段与 Mark Fell 的碎裂打击乐层层叠加，电子节拍在柏林学派与实验俱乐部之间游走。B 面交由 Ricardo Villalobos 接管，蜿蜒的极简脉冲与 Joe Talia、Will Guthrie 的现场鼓组交织，克拉夫特-Techno 逐渐蜕变为迪斯科融合，Keith Fullerton Whitman 的模块合成器试图将轨道推离正轨，Arto Lindsay 的吉他收尾则标志全曲进入爵士噪音的终极释放。十年之后回望，这张集合了多位重要音乐人参与的作品依然是独立厂牌 Black Truffle 美学理念的最佳入口。

items.body:
Holy moly, this is fire! Released by Heat Crimes in collaboration with Thessaloniki's Elhellell label, ‘Paradise Metal’ introduces the fretless electric guitar devotionals of Father Dionysios Tabakis, a 52 year old priest from the historic Greek city of Nafplio, who voices Byzantine church songs in a mix of amp worship hymns and outernational trance movements akin to Sir Richard Bishop or Sandy Bull via László Hortobágyi at Christian Love Forum’s sunday skool. WTF gear of the highest calibre…

‘Paradise Metal’ is one of many reasons why we keep reiterating: Heat Crimes is one of the best labels out there right now. At more than one point did we have to pinch ourselves at the the holy father’s procession of epiphanies effortlessly bridging ancient, microtonal Byzantine modes with DIY electronic modernism, often in jaw-dropping juxtapositions; sublime new age ambient to shoe-gazy basslines and mountaintop guitar shreds to techno incantations. Honestly it’s floored us in so many ways and is bound to exert the same effect with any of you lot, especially if you’re on a mission to sniff out incredible music from unknown margins.

The dozen songs speak richly to Father Dionysios Tabakis’ life immersed in the Orthodox church, and namely the historic Church of Panagitsa in Nafplio (Nativity of the Theotokos), one of the oldest and most beautiful in a city renowned as a centre of Greek faith. There, he has devoted a life to studying music and writing books, applying Athonite monastic wisdom to contemporary concerns of alienation, depression, and isolation in his writings -  which also feed directly into his extraordinary music. 

On a dozen songs the Holy Father proves as fluidly adept at a range of traditional Byzantine instruments (qanun, oud, cümbüş, Politikon tanbur, yali tanbur, ney, zurna, clarinet, Politiki lyra, Pontic lyra, kabak kemane) as his signature fretless guitar, favoured for its ability to feel out microtones - semi or quarter-tone pitches - closest to the human voice. The result is a level of emotional expression and harmonic colour that often escapes western modes, transcending a range of Asia Minor and Mediterranean styles from maqam to Greek traditional and Byzantine music with a disciplined but rapturous sense of transcendence.

Suffice it to say it all adds up to one of the most singular recordings we’ve heard in recent memory, knocking our heads clean off with flashbacks to the likes of Sandy Bull’s modal psych-folk, or even Sunn O))) x Julian Cope and Sun City Girls/Sir Richard Bishop ritualism in the first half, and traversing in the 2nd to astonishing sorts of techno impressionism, as with the THX string shear and choral chant of ‘TECHNO σε ΜΟΝΑΣΤΗΡΙ’ and a whole new definition of trance-techno, thru to bits that sound like a Greek Enya. 

100% brilliant, out there music.
items._genre: experimental / Byzantine / microtonal / world fusion / electronic
items._cn_summary: 希腊纳夫普利奥一位五十二岁东正教神父的跨界之作，将拜占庭教堂圣咏与无品电吉他、微分音调式结合，辅以卡龙琴、乌德、奈伊等多种西亚及地中海传统乐器。十二首歌曲横跨新世纪氛围、梦幻低音线、山顶吉他即兴段落与techno咒语式律动，在古代调式与DIY电子现代主义之间构建惊人的并置。作品以阿索斯修道院的智慧回应当代疏离、抑郁与孤独的主题，微分音的运用让情绪表达超越西方调式的局限。Heat Crimes与Elhellell联合发行，承载着来自希腊信仰中心的深厚传统，同时以出人意料的方式融入techno印象派与迷幻民谣元素。

items.body:
In physical stature and imaginative scope, Luc Ferrari’s 10 x CD / 11 Hour selection for INA GRM’s series presents a poetic building block of C.20th electronic music from the founding director of the GRM in 1958, presenting a unique art history spanning six decades of ingenious, beguiling soundcraft.

Part of a legendary series including titles by concrète pioneers Pierre Schaefer & Pierre Henry, plus weighty surveys of Bernrad Parmegiani, Éliane Radigue and François Bayle, this lavish boxset of Luc Ferrari’s work is a masterclass exploration of avant garde form and function that charts experimental music’s research and development during a radical phase. While even the notion of such a large storage device for sound was unimaginable when Ferrari began making his cut-up musical collages and sound poetry in the ‘50s, his ‘L’Œuvre Électronique’ covers the progression of musical technology and thought from its most laboriously executed origins, working with tape and raw blocks of sound, to the grander digital staging of his ‘90s and early ‘00s radio plays, plotted for multiple voices and spatialised landscapes. 

Collected, this set forms an incredible deep dive into art-music history where the materiality of sound is questioned and reconsidered in relief of its musical connotations, creating in the process a peerless body of work that better approximates the texture of dreams or the audness of waking life than any song, and has long informed the approach to sound organisation by a host of progressive artists, effectively bridging the conceptual precedents of Varèse and Cage and the contemporary futures projected by Lee Gamble or Valerio Tricoli.

The 98 tracks from 31 releases, clocking up just over 10 hours of recordings, delineate across decades following Ferrari’s studies with Messaien and Honegger in the mid ‘50s, and a period of illness that made him better acquainted with the radio receiver, and pioneers such as Schöneberg and Webern, to his co-founding of the Groupe de Recherches Musicales with Schaeffer and François-Bernard Mâche in 1958, and thru his landmark transformation of field recordings made on a Yugoslavian beach, and the ravishing abstractions of later electronic works. 

Until his passing, aged 76 in Arezzo, Italy, Ferrari remained ceaselessly active both in his own practice and teaching, and was revered as the poet of musique concrète. He bought a particularly gallic purview to the paradigm, especially when considered against the more hard-nosed academic pursuits of his peers, making singular use of vocals as an elusive or sometimes literal presence in his works in a way that others didn’t, and as such his works all hare a certain liminal quality that appears richly seductive to fans of fantasy storytelling as much as psychedelic soundtracks and sound as dreamfood imagery.

items._cn_summary: 此套盒装精选收录了法国电子音乐先驱吕克·费拉里跨越六十年的声音创作，涵盖98首作品、31张发行、总时长逾十小时。费拉里早年随梅西安与奥涅格学习，1958年共同创立音乐研究小组，后将田野录音技术引入音乐创作，其标志性的南斯拉夫海滩录音实验成为具体音乐领域的里程碑。作品从早期的磁带剪贴与声音拼贴起步，延伸至九十年代以降的数字广播剧，呈现声音物质性的多重解构与重组。作为皮埃尔·舍费尔与亨利一系的同代人物，费拉里以独特的诗意视角处理人声元素，使作品呈现出介于梦境与清醒听觉之间的质感，桥接了瓦雷兹与凯奇的概念先驱与当代实验音乐的多向可能。

items.body:
The classic 12 disc Parmegiani Box Set finally given a reissue by INA GRM, covering the majority of Parmegiani's musique concrète output recorded between 1964 and 2007. Is there a more important, influential, totemic single-artist collection in all of electronic music?

The Wire magazine described it as a "bargain price treasure chest....containing worlds of inexhaustible spaciousness and strangeness" and, indeed, listening through just some of the 12 cd's included you find yourself drawn into a multi-faceted world full of timeless treasure.

Parmegiani was mentored by the founding father of Musique Concrète, Pierre Schaeffer, who made use of technological advances that gave the world magnetic tape and microphones to pioneer a method taking everyday noise and transforming them into unrecognisable sounds, a style that became known as Acousmatic music. 

Parmegiani would go on to make use of these Acousmatic techniques in creating a body of work which is not only one of the most significant of the 20th century, but also hugely influential on a whole host of musical pioneers that would follow in his wake, with Christian Fennesz, Aphex Twin, Kode9 and Jim O'Rourke being notable disciples in the contemporary field. 

It’s hard to comprehend let alone articulate the immersive and often woozy effect of these recordings, ranging from eerie cut-out tape loops through to popular music plunderphonics and proto-distilled-dub that's impossible to absorb in one sitting. In short, L’Œuvre Musicale is one of the most impressive and important collections of electronic music you'll likely ever hear, but also one of the most rewarding.
items._genre: musique concrète / acousmatic / experimental electronic / tape music
items._cn_summary: 这是由INA GRM再版的Bernard Parmegiani十二碟盒装录音合辑，收录了1964至2007年间作者具象音乐创作的绝大部分作品。作者师从Pierre Schaeffer，继承了将日常声响转化为不可辨识音色的Acousmatic手法，发展出独特的磁带循环与拼贴美学。作品中既有诡谲的剪接磁带环，也有对流行音乐进行的拼贴解构，更有原始的dub实验痕迹。The Wire称其为"廉价珍宝箱"，因其声音空间感与奇异质感极为深邃。整盒录音展现了一位先驱如何用磁带技术与录音室逻辑，构建出超越时代的聆听体验，对Fennesz、Aphex Twin、Kode9、Jim O'Rourke等后辈影响深远。

items.body:
The Necks regroup on a staggering first new LP in three years, switching between skittering jazz to widescreen rollers with a breathtaking momentum - somewhere between classic Verve label, MvO Trio, This Heat and Oren Ambarchi's ensemble jams.

The Necks’ Chris Abrahams (piano, Hammond organ), Tony Buck (drums, percussion, electric guitar) and Lloyd Swanton (bass guitar, double bass) re-ignite a mesmerising minimalism on ‘Travel’, taken from very lightly edited and overdubbed recordings of their daily 20 minute warm-up/improv practice sessions. Now in their 34th year playing together, the Aussie unit’s fine-honed intuitions are fully apparent across four durational parts totalling 77 minutes sprawling across seemingly endless soundscapes that collapse into myriad genres.

Perfectly framed and suspended with beautifully buoyant mixing and engineering by long time collaborator Tim Whitten, ‘Travel’ is a swaggering statement by the modern masters of long-form jams. The elements are knit with a particularly smoked-out verve and swingeing flex in each part, stretching from what sounds like MvO Trio haunted by Jackie Mittoo on the extraordinary ‘Signal’, to an uncanny, streamlined echo of Ndikho Xaba and the Natives’ South African free jazz on ‘Forming’, before resembling Can emulating Brazilian jazz on ‘Imprinting’, and arriving at the heart-in-mouth tempest of snare rolls, escalating organ vamps and roving low end that brings the LP to a thunderous climax like some extended Alice Coltrane breakdown that leaves u tossed in mid air.

Sounding as lean and potent as they did on 1989’s debut LP ‘Sex’, they’re frankly showing off here, with ‘Travel’ registering as good a place as any to kick off your infatuation with one of the world’s greatest experimental units.
items._cn_summary: The Necks 历经三十四年合作的澳洲实验爵士三重奏，时隔三年推出新专辑，将每日二十分钟即兴热身录音经轻度剪辑与叠录后，延伸为四段总长七十七分钟的绵长声景。钢琴、 Hammond 风琴、低音吉他与鼓组在极简框架中展开高度默契的即兴对话，混合了迷幻爵士、南非自由爵士、巴西爵士与迷幻摇滚等多种色彩，以烟雾感十足的律动和延展的器乐张力贯穿始终。制作人 Tim Whitten 提供了宽裕而悬浮的混音质感，使各乐器层次保持饱满呼吸感。从开场灵巧的爵士律动到终曲类似 Alice Coltrane 崩裂式的风琴与军鼓风暴，专辑呈现了长期即兴团体罕见的结构掌控力与多变声部形态，既保留了首张专辑的精瘦与锋利，也展现了当代长篇即兴作品的高完成度。

items.body: To say that a work starts with a bang is a cliché, yet Boca De Acero definitely has an explosive intro. Not only that, the momentum on this five-movement duet remains taut till the final note. A collaboration between two singular musicians, the Argentinian vocalist Ines Terra and Uruguayan guitarist Santiago Bogacz, this album is entirely improvised and demonstrates a seamless camaraderie between them. This abstract, cinematic conversation has a shifting mood and thrilling twists and turns within the underlying harmonic narrative. Track “1” opens with fiery, angular guitar strums and Terra’s wordless vocal acrobatics. Terra makes her shouts and cries bounce off Bogacz’s strings with dramatic flair. The guitarist weaves a dense and dynamic soundscape around Terra’s chants. [Text Wrapping Break]Despite embracing dissonance, the pair maintains a subtle lyricism throughout their exchanges. The darkly hued “2” brims with mysticism. Terra’s rising and falling voice hauntingly floats over Bogacz’s sparse chords. The refrains that evolve with each repetition have a ritualistic feel, almost like the ceremonial liturgy of a long-forgotten ancient rite. With “3” the somber mood continues, becoming quieter and more nocturnesque. Terra softly whispers, and Bogacz plucks single notes that underscore the serenity of the mood. Their conversation takes on a sublime theatricality. Meanwhile, on “4” the two artists fully embrace mysticism as her throat singing and his hypnotic strums ebb and flow against a quiet backdrop, ending on a passionate note. The fifth piece features synthesizer sounds that distort the emotive and stimulating improvisation, creating a delightfully otherworldly atmosphere. The burgeoning piece melds the organic quality of the human voice with sharp, acerbic electronic vamps for a performance that is simultaneously stimulating and eerie. With Boca De Acero, Terra and Bogacz have undertaken a successful sonic experiment that is provocative and moving. It is also a much-needed glimpse into South America’s vibrant improvisational scene. That, much like the recording’s creators of this album, is unique, expressive, and fearless. Boca de acero by Inés Terra + Santiago Bogacz Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook

items._cn_summary: Boca De Acero 是阿根廷歌手 Ines Terra 与乌拉圭吉他手 Santiago Bogacz 的全即兴五乐章二重奏作品。整张专辑充满张力，开篇以爆炸性引子切入，至终曲保持紧绷的动能。Terra 使用无词的人声技巧，包括喊叫、哭诉、喉音唱法与耳语；Bogacz 则以吉他拨弦、扫弦及合成器音色构建多变的声音景观。两人在不和谐中维持微妙的抒情性，对话兼具电影感与戏剧性，氛围在神秘、阴郁、仪式感之间流动。第五乐章引入合成器元素，将人声的有机质感与尖锐电子音色融合，营造出既刺激又诡异的异世界氛围。专辑展现了南美即兴音乐场景的活力，是一次大胆且成功的声学实验。

items.body: If a tree falls in the forest, does it make a sound? And what if an entire forest falls? Around Here, The Birds Plant The Trees, inspired by a “clear-felled wasteland” in Leitrim, Ireland, amplifies these questions. In the digital era, it prompts an additional question: “When the liner notes are integral to the release, will listeners intuit the point?” We hope so, in the same manner as those hearing classical works over the centuries have gleaned the intentions of the composers, from “The Goldfinch” to The Four Seasons. In her first work for ensemble, Natalia Beylis uses different instruments to evoke “the rustle of beetles in the hedgerow, the squeak of a leaning Sitka spruce, a lone curlew’s call,” and her overall concern is that listeners will hear the richness of a richness of a landscape and be moved to protect it. While this landscape is incredibly specific: a single field on 12 December 2025, beginning at 6 a.m. ~ it could be any environment threatened by large multinational corporations, who swoop in to offer short-term recompense for long-term loss. Looking out over the field, Beylis notes the activity of a single blackbird, and later, an entire flock. Adding to the pathos is the fact that even birds are now endangered (for details, we recommend Robert Macfarlane & Jackie Morris’ The Book of Birds). If the music of the actual birds is inadequate to promote empathy, might music take up the cause? The alternative is to say nothing and to play nothing. As one might expect, the 51-minute piece is filled with intricate description and high drama. The cello’s low notes launch the piece in a reverent tone, considering at a field that once was a forest. As the other members of the string quartet join in, the nuance starts to develop. What began as drone becomes a harmonic suite with a distinctly Irish lilt. Then the first taps of percussion, like small creatures rustling through the grass, foraging for breakfast. A period of abstraction follows, during which every resident of field and forest receives their own spotlight. The blackbird eats and mates and cross-pollinates. The squirrels rush to and fro; the fox chases the shrew. All the while, the breeze threads through the branches of the hawthorn, creating a rhythm of leaves. The atmosphere seems peaceful until the thrums of the 15th minute, a soupçon of danger as most of the animals and instruments go into hiding. The contrast between presence and absence is integral to the composition. One feels the recession of sound as one might feel the destruction of trees. What was once lush becomes a hush, like the quietude of midday. Then the drone re-develops, a symbol of hope and regrowth. A vast cymbal strike like a gong at 32:07 interrupts the process, leaving only the drums and the wind in its wake. Willie Stewart’s work in this segment is enthralling; it sounds like architecture being built. But as the strings re-enter, are they busy as bees or as bulldozers? The listener is left to decide. Beylis initially planned to “write something to equal the harsh cacophony of the harvesting machines as they shred the nests of fledgling buzzards; to evoke the rumbling shaking noise I’d hear in bed at night as they crashed the huge trees they’d cut to the ground,” but relented for the sake of the blackbird. The dissonance that follows the drums suggests that the idea was not totally discarded. This makes the closing segment all the sweeter: consonance rising out of dissonance, form from chaos. The forest may have been leveled, but around here, the birds plant the trees. This being said, the story is not meant to encourage as much as it is to unsettle. Robert Plant once sang, “if there’s a bustle in your hedgerow, don’t be alarmed now.” Beylis has a different message: be alarmed. Be very alarmed. (Richard Allen)
items._genre: contemporary classical / modern composition / experimental / folk / field recording
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Natalia Beylis的首部室内乐作品，以爱尔兰Leitrim一片被皆伐的荒地为灵感，将一片特定田野的声音生态转化为51分钟的弦乐四重奏与打击乐合奏。低弦大提琴以虔诚的嗡鸣开篇，随后发展成具有爱尔兰风情的和声组曲；打击乐的轻敲模拟草间虫豸的窸窣，每一种田野与森林中的生灵都获得属于自己的独白段落——黑鹂觅食、松鼠奔走、狐狸追逐鼩鼩。乐曲中段声音的退场如林木被伐后的寂静，镲的巨响则如警钟。最后弦乐重新涌入，作为重生与希望的象征。作品的核心命题是：当自然的鸟鸣不足以唤起人类的共情，音乐能否替而代之，唤醒对环境破坏的抵抗。

items.excerpt: Pentagrams Of Discordia seem to vaporize sound itself, blending traces of past, present, and future until their downtempo worlds begin to intertwine. items.body: Pentagrams Of Discordia seem to vaporize sound itself, blending traces of past, present, and future until their downtempo worlds begin to intertwine. Beats become memories, melodies become distant signals, and atmosphere takes over as the guiding force. Cryptic chapters buried deep within a book of shadows   Out of nowhere, and perhaps because of our curiosity about all things Pentagrams Of Discordia, Whispers About Radiance slips into view through three long-form pieces of nostalgic, downtempo analog production that feel less like compositions and more like an escape through lost time. Melancholic yet forward-thinking, propelled by atmosphere but steered by broken, disheveled beats, meandering tone clusters, and fractured rhythms, this sampler may showcase only three compositions, but it feels more like several cryptic chapters buried deep within a book of shadows. Darkness and sadness blur around the edges, as though POD can seamlessly traverse time and space, moving between half-remembered places and dream worlds without ever fully settling in one. Each chapter carries remarkable depth; off-kilter synths intertwine with shattered percussion while uplifting reverse-looped melodies and degraded rhythms slowly dissolve, reappear, and drift away like faded memories or solitary wanderings down memory lane. Nothing remains entirely fixed; sounds and voices emerge from the ha​ze, briefly take shape, then recede, leaving behind the feeling of having remembered something that never quite happened. These semi-pastiche soundtracks, steeped in BOC-laden sonic syrup and kaleidoscopic drift, form another wonderful collection for those who find comfort in music that refuses to reveal everything at once. Voices, samples, pulsing old-school beats, melodies, and wandering analog sequences trace a peculiar musical trajectory, buried beneath darkness yet constantly peering toward the light. Aptly titled, the album seems to whisper a transmission of light and energy from somewhere just beyond our vision, a surface deliberately left indistinct, perhaps because it was never meant to be fully understood. Circling through patterns that gradually mutate rather than resolve :: The slow-motion emotion of opener “Slowing of Evolution” unfolds across 18 minutes, conjuring fantastical stages of eroded sound that gradually take root and nurture the soul. Its movement is patient, but never static, allowing ambient passages and rhythmic fragments to guide one another through a landscape that feels both ancient and strangely futuristic. “Refrain of Dusk” maintains that slow-churning momentum, rugged drums collapsing into melodic shifts and subtle transitions while atmosphere remains firmly at its core. There is a sense of forward motion here, though it arrives more like drifting than traveling. Like reliving childhood memories, a few minutes at a time—waking up from one only to slowly fade into another. Closing piece “Loops of Entropy” is perhaps the most structured of the three, built around heavier-duty breaks and a more pronounced sense of mood. Its title quite literally evokes “cyclic processes or recursive loops tied to disorder and uncertainty,” and the music follows suit, circling through patterns that gradually mutate rather than resolve. What begins as something comparatively grounded slowly fragments, dissolving back into ambient propulsion. By the closing chapter, POD seem to vaporize sound itself, blending traces of past, present, and future until their downtempo worlds begin to intertwine. Beats become memories, melodies become distant signals, and atmosphere takes over as the guiding force. Eventually, all that remains is the urge to return and listen again, following layer upon layer as they hypnotize, unsettle, and reflect back some of the finest soundscapes and sound-scrapes we’ve heard this year. Whispers About Radiance (Sampler) is a precursor to the forthcoming August 28, 2026 album. [Bandcamp]  The post Pentagrams Of Discordia :: Whispers About Radiance (Sampler) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._genre: downtempo / experimental electronic / dark ambient / IDM
items._cn_summary: Pentagrams Of Discordia的这张采样专辑以三首长篇作品构建了一个模糊时空界限的声音世界。制作以低保真模拟合成器、碎裂的打击节奏和迷蒙的氛围为核心，声音不断浮现又消散，像未曾真正发生的记忆。慢速的节奏推进与氛围段落交替出现，合成器音色偏离常规，旋律以反向循环和降质处理的方式漂移，整体散发着忧郁与暗色调。评论特别提到作品与Boards of Canada式的声景有密切关联，强调其在模拟质感与电子实验之间的平衡。专辑不急于给出明确表达，而是通过持续演变的声音纹理邀请听众进入一种半梦半醒的聆听状态，适合在安静环境中长时间沉浸式体验。

All secreted to tape on
items.body:
Anyone smote by DINTE’s ‘Begena Songs…’ will be properly enchanted by this more expansive - yet still intimate - suite of snapshots from Ethiopia, ’71, spanning the unique, twanging harp sound thru to Amharic poetry, Afar chants, and spellbinding flutes dances

One that catches the breath with seldom felt sensations, ‘Ethiopian Musics 1971’ patently owes as much to the incredible performers as their faithful representation in Ragnar Johnson & Ralph Harrisson’s recordings. All secreted to tape on a Uher Report L stereo reel-to-reel recorder, they epitomise an era of ethnomusicological preservation, when the likes of labels such as Lyrichord and  Folkways were already decades deep “in the field”, documenting long-held traditions practically untouched by an encroaching, western modernity. And perhaps most crucially, the recordings beautifully render the acoustic settings and vivid vibes with an immersive quality in stark opposition to the era of dry, so-called audiophile studio recordings of ethnic musics to come - all the better for immersing in this wonderfully unfamiliar world.

The abundance of singular tones and strong, rare feels they produce is quite staggering to our northern english ears, and we reckon also for anyone else, for that matter. Opening to a joyful couplet of a bluesy ’Song about the beauty of women’, and the almost shanty-like swing and hard rhythm of ’Tej Beit Song’, the set reels to distinctive pieces of Ethiopian Christian song set to begena, or ‘Harp of David’, buzz, and a landscape-scale, 13 minute ‘Love Song (Mary Armede)’. A gripping ‘Drum Song (Jigsaw)’ will be mana to rhythm fiends, and a number of standout flute pieces reprise the frisson of our first encounter with this discipline on Sublime Freq’s ‘Staring into the Sun - Ethiopian Tribal Music’ set of 2012, most potently on the pluming twin pipes of the ‘Fila Flute Dance’ parts, whilst the pentatonic craar (6-stringed lyre) parts surely strike nerves for lovers of the rawest blues, and hail the liberated legacy of Mary Armede, a folk singer-fashion designer of Azmari heritage who surely warrants further investigation. 

No doubt this is one of the most striking archival discoveries of 2026, acutely advised to anyone enchanted with music from this corner of the world from Éthiopiques to begena harp, thru to Ragnar Johnson’s other arenas of research for Ideologic Organ in Yemen or Papua New Guinea. Dive in without delay.

items._cn_summary: 这张1971年录制于埃塞俄比亚的田野录音合集收录了贝吉纳竖琴、阿姆哈拉诗歌、阿法尔吟唱及各种笛舞等多样化的传统音乐形态，由Ragnar Johnson与Ralph Harrisson使用Uher Report L立体声盘式录音机在实地完成。录音以沉浸式声学质感保存了未被西方现代性侵蚀的古老传统，与后来干涩的录音棚民族音乐形成鲜明对比。专辑开篇以歌颂女性之美的布鲁斯风格作品和节奏强烈的Tej Beit之歌展开，随后涵盖埃塞俄比亚基督教圣歌、长达13分钟的玛丽亚·阿梅德情歌、引人入胜的鼓乐以及六弦琴的原始布鲁斯质感。整张合集展现了这一时期民族音乐学家深入田野进行抢救性录音的工作方式，为埃塞俄比亚传统音乐保存了珍贵的声学文献。

items.body:
Colin Stetson’s breakthrough album of gripping bass sax innovations still buzzes like few others.

In 2007 ‘New History Warfare Vol.1’ asserted Stetson as an indomitable player of wind instruments, here letting off on Alto, Baritone and Bass Saxophones, plus Clarinet, in a deftly muscular display of his skills which had previously been employed on record and in live tours for Arcade Fire, Tom Waits, Bon Iver, LCD Soundsystem and whoever the heck else needed a set of lungs as good as a blacksmith’s bellows.

While perhaps best known for wielding a massive Bass Saxophone that's responsible for some of the wildest sounds on this album, Stetson proves to be a sensitive beast capable of articulating the instrument’s full range tonal in his own voice, which variously comes out resembling a purring big cat and the dying wildebeest it just stalked, attacked and slaughtered in ‘Time Is Advancing With Fitful Irregularity’, while he uses the same broad tone to describe natural scenes as textured with soil and moisture and wind as an Anne Guthrie piece in ‘As a Bird or Branch’, while ‘Nobu Take’ sounds like a manic 8-bit computer game soundtrack and ’Tiger Tiger Crane’ adds a tight percussive workout for good measure, but trust its all acoustic, instrumental, hands-on, somehow not processed. 

Still a stonking good record, this, ripe for re/discovery.
items._genre: free improvisation / experimental / avant-garde jazz / contemporary classical
items._cn_summary: Colin Stetson 的首张突破性专辑以低音萨克斯为核心，辅以中音、次中音萨克斯与单簧管，在完全原声、纯器乐的框架下展开独奏式即兴演奏。他运用循环呼吸技术，使单一乐器层层叠加出厚重的音墙质感。专辑涵盖多种情绪光谱：从粗犷暴烈的低频咆哮到细腻敏感的呼吸式叙事，每首曲目都有独特的角色设定——有的如狩猎中的大型猫科动物，有的如湿润泥土与风声交织的自然音景，有的则被形容为疯狂的 8 位电脑游戏配乐。整张专辑强调纯粹的物理演奏，没有任何电子处理，展现了非常规管乐器在独奏语境下所能达到的极限表现力与情感跨度。

items.body:
Effortlessly easy on the ear and yet still somehow fathoms-deep, Tara Clerkin Trio’s latest is their most refined and fully-formed transmission yet, mining a precious sweetspot between chamber-jazz, Plone-style bric-a-brac electronics, Crescent’s lo-fi reveries and the urban pressure of the Young Echo collective, unpicking decades of British musical history in the process. Trust, it’s a special one.

Like every great band, TCT know their history. They've grown up with and formed their identity in the shadow of Bristol's musical lore, whether it's The Pop Group, Massive Attack or Flying Saucer Attack, and when they use traceable elements, it feels like a believable part of their DNA. Thankfully, they meaningfully add to that narrative too, not adapting an aesthetic for easy consumption. Part of this might be down to their makeup; they formed in the late 20-teens from the ashes of the Tara Clerkin Band, a larger ensemble that Clerkin had put together to expand the scope of her folk-y pop compositions. And when most of the members moved on, stepbrothers Sunny-Joe Paradiso and Patrick Benjamin stuck around to see where the road might lead. All "proper" players, they've traditionally let their songs appear from what sounds like loose, casual improvisations, like you're tuned into Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society' band running through Laika's 'Silver Apples of the Moon'.

So you get a song like the brilliant 'Ups & Downs', that simmers for a good four minutes with wheezing harmonium, double bass and clarinet, percussion just rumbling in the background somewhere, before a jerky sampled beat, Mellotron strings and Clerkin's voice would have you thinking Matt Elliott's behind the boards. But 'Somewhere Good' is also remarkably tight when it needs to be, walking a tightrope between easy breezy and meticulous with acrobatic skill. Opener 'Lake Walk', for example, sounds intentionally naive, jammed out loosely on synthesised and real woodwind that's caught in a vortex of Space Echo, before 'Lazy Daisy' cuts it short with its more ordered (but still kinda slouchy) beat-heavy dreampop atmosphere. It's where the album's shape really coagulates, between Broadcast's dramatic early EPs (back when they were touring with Plone) and Pram's best shit, just lightly tweezed at the edges, its creases relaxed to fit in with Laila Sakini's quietly genius 'Paloma'. And that mood carries the record even when Clerkin's voice - pursed into a soulful croon or a lackadaisical murmur - vanishes completely. One of the most gripping moments arrives with 'There Was a Nice Sunset', effortlessly matching slowcore drums with piano flourishes and synths, locking into the same general feeling but widening the boundaries, nodding to Adrian Sherwood's lysergic work on Creation Rebel's 'Starship Africa'. 

There's years of British musical history baked into this stuff, and yet it feels wholly new.
items._genre: experimental jazz / lo-fi electronica / chamber jazz / dream pop
items._cn_summary: Tara Clerkin Trio 在这张专辑中以松散即兴为核心方法，从室内爵士的器乐编制出发，融入管风琴、单簧管、采样节拍与空间回声效果，形成松弛与精密并存的声场结构。乐队源自布里斯托丰富的音乐谱系——从 The Pop Group 到 Young Echo——但不复制既有美学，而是将慢核、民谣流行与迷幻电子的语汇重组为带有个人印记的声音。全专辑呈现碎片化的拼贴气质，乐曲常在数分钟的酝酿后才展开核心段落，器乐层次与录音质感的细节是聆听关键。整体作品既扎根于英国独立音乐传统，又展现出向新方向延伸的可能。

items.body:
Pushing back against "Acid Nostalgia", Lawrence English dreams of a moonlit future on 'The Rest is My Ghost', bringing in assistance from a heap of collaborators, including Mats Gustafsson, Tony Buck, Chris Abrahams, Rully Shabara, Norman Westberg and Lena Ito.

Having fully deconstructed his persona on 2022's 'Approach', looking back to his formative influences - William Gibson's 'Neuromancer' and Yoshihisa Tagami's sci-fi manga 'Grey' - English was left with a conundrum that he solved by taking a step back. Last year's 'Even the Horizon Knows its Bounds' was billed as a grand collaborative effort, performed by a litany of English's associates and imagined as an "atmospheric tint" for the Naala Badu building at the Art Gallery of New South Wales. 'The Rest is My Ghost' is very different; more radical and more overtly political than its predecessors, more in line with 2014's charged 'Wilderness of Mirrors' and its brilliant follow-up 'Cruel Optimism', the album takes aim at the contemporary obsession with nostalgia. Provoked by a conversation with Adam Curtis and driven by texts from Mark Fisher, JG Ballard, Katsuhiro Otomo, Franco Berardi, Kate Crawford and Alexie Yurchak and cultural architectural realities like the loss of Los Angeles' signature street lamps and Japan's Metabolists, English searches for a "political projection of nostalgia" that he can subsequently rupture. "Like acid poured onto a surface," he writes. "this use of nostalgia seeks to erode and smooth out the complexity and texture of lived connection and longing, which has until recently guided contemplations of nostalgia."

He's talking about the difference between dreaming of your own past and being sold a neatly packaged pseudo-reality, its highs and lows removed to ease the ingestion. Nobody would argue that 'Stranger Things', for example, wasn't nostalgic, but is its high concept fun comparable with any of its direct influences? Even its soundtrack pales alongside pretty standard straight-to-VHS fodder of the era, it's just cleaner, zippier and more shareable. And the more it dragged on, the less vital it became - a Gen X-core soap opera with eerily familiar visual cues. To represent this concept musically, English moves away from the dense distortions you might expect and instead collects up instrumental performances from a wide swathe of players. But perusing the personnel list and projecting your expectations on the material is part of the process. English obscures everything very purposefully, shrouding the instrumentation in reverb and midnight gusts. If seeing names like Swans' Thor Harris and pedal steel player Chuck Johnson gives you pause, that's the point. English engages in his own hauntological process, extracting the essence from the stems and imprinting it on his soundscapes. He's not eroding the material by any means, but searching out the triggers that play on the imagination, inspiring futures that have never been more difficult to grasp.

And if it sounds dark, it's really not supposed to. Listen through the nocturnal hums and gentle, thrumming ambiance and you'll discover more than you bargained for - even a glimmer of hope. The result is a record that lands somewhere between Les Disques du Crépuscule's post-classical gear, Eno's fourth world experiments with John Hassell and Alan Lamb's influential sound art.
items._cn_summary: Lawrence English 延续其声音艺术探索，与多位跨领域音乐人合作，将个人独奏项目拓展为集体创作。专辑以'酸蚀怀旧'为概念，对抗当下文化中被商品化的怀旧情绪，通过大量混响与深夜氛围包裹乐器演奏，故意模糊演奏者身份。文本引用了多位思想家与建筑师，从威廉·吉布森的《神经漫游者》到日本新陈代谢派的建筑理念，探讨集体记忆如何被抹平与重塑。音乐上摒弃了以往密集的失真处理，转而收集广泛的器乐演奏素材，再以自己的声景处理方式进行'幽灵化'再加工，邀请听众在不知演奏者身份的状态下纯粹体验声响本身。专辑延续了作者对政治性与空间感的高度关注，在延续早期作品锋芒的同时开辟了新的协作路径。

items.body:
Compiling rare-as-hen's-teeth material from iconic Aotearoa/New Zealand label World Resources, 'Fully Nowhere' presents four sides of scuzzy lo-fi rock, drone, noise pop and improv from a tight cadre of the country's most prolific outsiders.

Established in the 1990s in Wellington, World Resources was a DIY label that specialised in tapes and micro-edition lathe-cut 7" singles and the home of Donald Smith, Paul Toohey and Tony McGurk's long-running free noise/drone band Surface of the Earth. It's an imprint that helped impact its region's knottiest outsider surges, so World of Echo does us a favor here by scraping together some of its rarest and most enduring sides, assembling a 25-track collection of some of the best basement drone and most surreal noise pop that's ever emerged from the Southern Hemisphere. The anthology begins in 1994 with two 7"s from Gorgecop, a short-lived solo project from Toohey. And already we're in impressive territory, with slashy grot-rock gear that wouldn't be out of place alongside The Shadow Ring and waved kosmische synth experiments that have more in common with the Dusseldorf wave. 

Donald Smith's Lucky Stars project yanks us back down to earth with the surprisingly bright and breezy 'Winter Call' a track that's so deliciously lo-fi that its drum machine beat barely cracks a faint pulse. Side B houses the grimy 'Hospital' and 'Smell of a Man's Room' from McGurk's Sewer solo project, tracks that originally appeared in 1995 on lathe cut of just 20 units that apparently never left his flat, and New Zealand Guitar Orchestra, a collaborative project between Surface of the Earth and Dress, have their two album releases condensed into a long stretch of submerged noise and interference that's worth the asking price alone. Of course, Surface of the Earth have to appear at some point and their track 'Shield' rounds up the side, with the brilliantly faded 'Commandcom' opening the next. Here, the trio's work is contextualized alongside their solo experiments, work as K-Group, Sewer and Destrifan that helps piece together a past, present and future of three DIY icons.
items._genre: lo-fi drone / noise pop / DIY experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由World of Echo厂牌整理，收录了来自新西兰Aotearoa传奇DIY厂牌World Resources在1990年代以来的稀有作品，共25首曲目横跨四张黑胶面。内容涵盖低保真摇滚、嗡鸣、噪响流行与即兴创作，主要围绕Paul Toohey、Donald Smith与Tony McGurk三位核心人物展开，包括Toohey的Gorgecop独奏项目、Sewer极端噪响作品，以及Surface of the Earth乐队的多首曲目。合辑梳理了三位音乐人的独立创作脉络及其合作项目，将微版限量首版、母带切割单曲等珍贵素材整合呈现，既是对新西兰地下音乐场景的历史性档案整理，也是对南半球实验音乐版图的补充。

items.body:
Greek harpist and composer Sissi Rada interprets the music of Richard Wagner and Johannes Brahms with unfathomable levels of detail and charm, resulting in one of the most gorgeously executed records of the year. Trust - it’s fully essential listening FFO Joanna Newsom, Svitlana Nianio, Kate Bush, Delphine Dora, Nikos Mamangakis…​

Sissi Makropoulou has been pinging our radar for a while now, but especially hard since 2024's Stroom-released 'Aporia' and that dazzling ‘Demeter In Aexone’ album that properly locked us in to her brand of uncanny avant dream-folk, a highly distinctive signature sound she developed even further on the fantastic 'Nana Butu' earlier this year. She’s a serial collaborator - with Lena Platonos, Brian Eno, Christina Vantzou, Jay Glass Dubs -  even Lee "Scratch" Perry -  all the while composing chamber music on the side. And It's that latter practice that comes to the fore on ‘Serious Songs’ singing in German while attacking Wagner's chilly 'Fünf Gedichte für eine Frauenstimme' (Five Poems for a Female Voice) on the A side, and Brahms' pious 'Vier ernste Gesänge' (Four Serious Songs) on the flip. As you'd expect, it isn't just a simple recital; with harp and voice the focal points, packed out with winding, nebulous arrangements and perspicacious references to avant-garde musical history, integrating dissonant orchestral elements, prepared piano, opera, classical guitar, environmental sounds and foreboding oscillations  - with an exquisite ear for detail.

Oddly for music this tranquil, it benefits from increased volume - at least a level where you can marvel at the array of tiny, unusual production flourishes. And it's a suite that grows and grows. On 'Wesendonck 1’, she opens with voice and harp recalling Joanna Newsom's folk-inspired song cycle 'Ys'. But as the piece develops, she begins to slowly show her hand, introducing harmonic, hypnotic effects to blur the edges. The result is discombobulating in the best way, sounding as dreamy as Julee Cruise's 'Floating into the Night' while somehow still remaining true to the source material. The drama continues to build on 'Wesendonck 2', her delivery of the words - written by poet Mathilde Wesendonck who Wagner was famously besotted with - fittingly dramatic, assisted by brass and grinding drums broken occasionally by moments of ineffable beauty. On 'Wesendonck 4', Makropoulou augments the production with metallophone chimes, fixing sequences with growling synths and heavily processed cries.

Sissi plays a remarkable sleight of hand on the flip. Beginning conservatively, she introduces Brahms' cycle of Lutheran biblical readings with a celestial harp and a gently experimental vocal, pitch shifted to a screwed conclusion. On 'Brahms 2', her performance is kinked by disorienting concrète-style operatic spools that pull us into another musical timeline entirely. She is so confident with her subject matter - whether it's the classical canon, folk, electronic or neue musik - that it all sounds like a natural extension of her practice, converging into something that fully defies categorisation.

Anyway, words don’t really do it for this one. Just give it a spin and you’ll soon melt into it, one of the most quietly startling albums released this year.
items._cn_summary: 希腊竖琴演奏家与作曲家Sissi Rada以竖琴与人声为核心，重新诠释瓦格纳与勃拉姆斯的经典声乐作品。专辑以德语演唱，融合不协和管弦元素、预置钢琴、歌剧咏叹、古典吉他、环境声响与低频振荡，将19世纪浪漫主义文本转化为模糊梦境与清醒现实边界的听觉体验。她对声音细节有着极强的把控，专辑在音量提升后展现出更为丰富的制作层次。整体呈现出一种不安的催眠感，既忠于原作的精神内核，又以前卫手法彻底重塑。评论明确将其列为年度最出色的唱片之一。

items.album: life is beautiful records: veneration for the sacred action

items.body:
Enigmatic label/collective life is beautiful fully establishes its lore on a colossal 3LP sprawl: 39 tracks of whimsical outsider biz arcing from lo-fi strums to asymmetric pop, jazz improv, poetry, noise, abstract hip-hop, spoken word and whatever else captures the thing, from artists you'll know and a fair few you won’t, featuring Bianca Scout, aloisius, VOICE ACTOR, James Massiah, Kenichi Iwasa, THE NARRATOR, Isaiah Hull, Pretty V and many, many more.

A self-styled gesamtkunstwerk, life is beautiful was established by aloisius in 2022 as a radio show, before turning into a collective, a series of live performances, and then inevitably a record label a year later. Their first comp makes some attempt to pull all their various strands into something cohesive, but like many of the best collectives - Mica Levi’s Curl crew for example - so much of the beauty and joy comes from following the breadcrumb trail deep into wherever they take you. This is a label, after all, that dumped their demos and experiments ("resources and inspiration") on a file exchange portal on their own site, so you get the idea that nothing is quite fixed, and there are no easy answers - just the pleasure of tagging along for the ride.

The set opens with tracks from each of the founders, who establish the label's core sound. NWAKKE begins with 'i need you in a positive way', a cloudy hypnagogic R&B marvel that juxtaposes cool-headed vocal runs with tape-fucked field recordings and piano. Then, the mic's handed to Amber Joy, aka THE NARRATOR, who also serves as the label's artistic director; on 'SUDDENLY', she oozes a skittish post-everything collage that chops cheap synths and choral vocals into a dreamy modern hymn. aloisus' 'you are god' runs out of its stuck groove as if it emerges from the very same thought, blurring gospel moans across LinnDrum loops. Bianca Scout hands us a taster of her collaborative work with London's Cajm on the hypnotic 'Welcome to Hello', while poet Isaiah Hull teams up with y+Your for the wonked 'vampire money'.

Basically there's a whole record of music from the crew before 'veneration...' even begins in earnest, and it only gets better from here, running through aesthetic experiments from multi-instrumentalist Kenichi Iwasa, self-styled "beat wizard" psychedelic ensemble. (who's one half of Brum's Everything is Psychedelic with Tony Bontana) and Thom Dehli before we reach the compilation's crown jewel, a 21-minute live jam from okk70 ensemble. We can't tell you exactly who's playing, but it's worth the price of entry alone, a squirming slo-mo jazz side that gets to the roots of the life is beautiful sound - like some cross between ’87 era Prince and Oren Ambarchi’s Ghosted Trio, except deep in the basement. Elsewhere, there's a chewably eccentric solo moment from Bianca Scout ('superscribe 24'), a phenomenally moody collaboration between VOICE ACTOR and aloisius ('24'), a spirited, lo-fi transmission from London's josiane pozi and a deeper than deep jam from orchestra379, aloisius' "collective improvisation project" that's featured artists like Ben Vince, Kenichi Iwasa and abi asisa. 

Label comps are often a slog but this one's stuffed to the gills with genuinely creative experimentation from some of the scene's most interesting outsiders, the sprawl really does come close to harnessing the vibe.

items.body:
Key Chicago house architect Ron Trent departs the club for the bedroom under new alias La Marr, a new vent for his most romantic, sublime soundscapes, warmly advised FFO Detroit Escalator Company, Terre Thaemlitz, Wally Badarou, Klaus Schulze, MvO Trio

Light candles/incense and scatter petals for optimal effect when immersing in La Marr’s debut ‘Mood Programs’ EP, which finds a perfect home nestled amid Music From Memory’s precious, timeline-twining cuts of new age ambient, kosmiche, and Balearic wist. It’s also a natural, logical progression from the sort of depths usually secreted in Trent’s albums, but here given full sides to unfurl their functions, which we’re sure will also sound dead tasty, syrupy slow, on 33-not-45. 

He paints the lushest 12 min panorama of elliptical stereo pads, floating organ cloud structures and skin-stroke arps in ‘Good Magic’, edging on similar terrain to Terre Thaemlitz’s golden revision of Tangerine Dream’s ‘Love on a Real Train’, where a fine line of hand played drums emphasises the swaying groove - swooning either bed-ways or a little rug-cut, depending on your disposition - before ‘Clear’ hustles a palette of the slinkiest Afro-Latinate, Brazilian rhythms under big, dusky skies, hinting at Manuel Göttsching via MvO Trio. 

Your ears do not deceive you: this one is proper lush.
items._genre: ambient / deep house / new age / kosmische
items._cn_summary: 芝加哥house元老Ron Trent以La Marr新身份推出的首张EP《Mood Programs》，将俱乐部律动转化为卧室聆听的私密空间。整张作品横跨十二分钟级别的长篇架构，以椭圆形立体声pad、漂浮管风琴云层与皮肤触感般的琶音构建出极致浪漫的声景，融汇新世纪ambient、krautrock电子与巴利阿里式的沉思气质。'Good Magic'以手打鼓点强调摇摆律动，可卧可舞；'Clear'则引入非洲-拉丁与巴西节奏律动，在黄昏般的天际线下铺展细腻纹理。整体制作强调33转慢速聆听的黏稠质感，是Trent创作脉络中向纵深拓展的逻辑延伸。

items.body:
Lolina's back with an insouciant and uncharacteristically vinegary barrage of scandalous whispers that arrive dressed as a tribute to Gossip Girl, backed up with asymmetrical remixes from Arca and NEW YORK.

On 'gg', Lolina reminisces about broken dreams and heartbreak. "That's one secret I will never tell," she promises, over smudgy, time-stretched drums and muggy organs. "Let's get another drink, or do you think I should be sober for what I am about to say?" It's a sonic side-eye that may or may not be historical and the lore's only extended by the cryptic press release (provided by Kaitlin Simotics) and the two reworks of Lolina's original.

London duo NEW YORK channel Lolina's energy into pop, singing the refrain and beefing the casual charm up with an electroid bassline, while Arca heads off-world, using Lolina's puzzling narrative to inspire her most gaseous track since her run with Björk. Digital harps are interrupted with glitches, and Lolina's words are slowed against syrupy OPN-like chipmunked chorals that coalesce into a symphonic crescendo...
items._genre: experimental electronic / glitch / art pop / ambient
items._cn_summary: Lolina以《Gossip Girl》为灵感起点，将破碎的情感记忆编织成一组缠绕的音景。专辑以模糊、失真拉伸的鼓机与潮湿的管风琴为底色，喃喃低语般的歌词穿梭其中，营造出若即若离的私密氛围。Arca的混音将原有叙事推至失重般的空间感，数码竖琴被故障碎片打断，人声在OPN式的加速合唱中消解，最终汇入交响化的渐强；NEW YORK的版本则将松弛气质注入流行骨架，电子贝斯线赋予随意魅力以重量感。两个remix版本形成鲜明对照——一端是轻盈的流行转译，另一端是气态化的星际漂流。整张作品在致敬与解构之间游走，模糊了流行引用与前卫实验的边界。

items.body: Luca Young crafts a hypnagogic birthing enclosure in the space created by this music, a space open for manifesting further gifts of reflective imagination. A sun shower appears, a brief trickle of luminescent moments Infinite Lovers, Pt. I by Luca Young   Electric guitar glitch swims in out of phase and out of focus photographs recovered from a forgotten SD card on the first song, “Welcome to the Other Side.” It reminds me of the skipping CDs used by the likes of Oval, clicks stuttering over top of field recordings of what sound like an airport or train station (a place of departure and return). It’s arrival music from the place we’ve departed from. These mesmeric textured loops are structured around they hypnotic guitar lines, themselves looping. All cascade and oscillate into the fog of timbral static coming off the Pacific. A disconsolate chord bathed in tape hiss and pitch shifted down starts “Pygmy Song.” The listening mind is teased by moments of reversed loops and the slide of fingers across the strings while glassy electronics appear for brief seconds in moments of fragility. Voices in staccato are cut and chopped alongside noisy high pitched tones who never overstay their welcome. It’s the music of dream memory trying to be captured and held onto, slipping away before it is fully grasped. On “7073” pensive upbeat strings meet with bo​uncing ball sounds and echo effects before swimming into crystalline pools of translucent electro refraction. Sounds of wave release the surf to the shore, and liquid textures. Small schools of musical fish swarm together for a moment, then separate in the drift of gentle abstract pulses and beats, the glitter of tiny notes surfacing for a second and then disappearing back into the deep. A sun shower appears, a brief trickle of luminescent moments. Directing the awakening of energy at the base of the spine :: The sound of planes rising or descending and further airport like sounds merge in a miasmic gloop at the beginning of “Kundalini.” The woman’s voice over the loudspeaker is comforting, directing the awakening of energy at the base of the spine, third eye subtly tingling by the luminescent vibrations. Further voices seem to be run through a gated sequencer, garbled through formant filters, language reduced to phonemes in a downtempo melodic style then disappears along the drift of a smoothly changing line. Infinity is in the distance. Part I of Infinite Lovers ends with the fifth track, “Ethiopia.” It’s starts with the ripple of tinkling pianos before building up successive pressure with louder playing, swoops of textural noise, warbling sonic transformations, glitch patterns, and long sweeps of filled with emotional grain. On this release Luca Young “was stepping into new territory artistically, moving away from a previous project. I decided to release this music under my given name, shedding an old artistic identity. It felt like the right move — a more honest expression of the kind of music I wanted to make.” The music is honest and unpretentious, warm and inviting. Leaving the skin of the old projects behind, he takes the listener on a voyage to the other side. It will be exciting to hear what comes with Part II. Infinite Lovers, Pt. I is available on Lōʻihi. [Bandcamp] Infinite Lovers, Pt. I by Luca YoungThe post Luca Young :: Infinite Lovers, Pt. I (Lōʻihi) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑构建了一个催眠般的声场，电吉他glitch与相位偏移效果穿梭于失焦的录音片段之间，让人联想到Oval时代的跳碟质感。录音素材取自机场、火车站等过渡性场所，配以磁带嘶声、逆向循环与玻璃质感的电子碎片，营造出试图被抓住又不断消散的梦境记忆。弦乐片段与弹跳声效汇入水晶般透明的电子折射层，海浪声与液态质感交叠，小鱼群般的音符短暂浮现又消失。整体从太平洋的音色静态中诞生，融合灵性意象与终端广播人声，经由formant滤波器处理后语言简化为音素。钢琴涟漪、质地噪声与情感颗粒感的声波扫描作为终曲收束，是一次对旧艺术身份的剥离与诚实的创作转型。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — The serial production aimed to expose the artifice behind the image, a concept applicable to any work conveying an underlying message. In this instance, it is music... which, through repetition, reveals itself to be more than it initially appeared. The cover of Taking Tiger Mountain (By Strategy) offers a clue as to what is going on. Several things happen simultaneously. Eno's calm vocals on "Burning Airlines Give You So Much More" head in one direction, while the guitars perform a different function; they are superimposed layers, much like Andy Warhol's serial-style photographs. The repetitive modal texture is merely the starting point for this game of Chinese boxes, which, when opened, reveal something different, something new. Something about "Back In Judy's Jungle" reminds me of those strange pop songs by 60s psychedelic bands, tracks with a circus-like atmosphere, such as Pink Floyd's "See Emily Play.""The Fat Lady of Limbourg" is more futuristic, closer to Krautrock and quintessentially Eno, featuring the songwriting style and vocal approach that remain constant regardless of the musical vehicle. After all, there is the playful, simpler Eno, or rather, a simplicity that emerges from complexity, and the openly experimental Eno, with echoes of Roxy Music in the mix. The track features electronic effects and Andy Mackay on saxophone, sounding like the wind-instrument simulators Eno would use later in his career (on Nerve Net, 1992), which once again interrupt and fracture the tempo. Nothing here is quite what it seems.Mother Whale Eyeless features Phil Collins on drums, a longtime friend of Eno who, at the time, was eager to collaborate on any experimental project that came along. Their experimental sensibilities meshed well, allowing them to find the spaces to transform the drums into yet another melodic instrument; they introduced variations that added color and diverse pitch ranges to the track, complementing the work done on guitar, given Phil Manzanera's presence throughout the album. Polly Eltes' guest vocals enhance those aforementioned higher registers... especially since the bass line later brings the pitch back down.The Great Pretender returns with dark Krautrock; we give thanks for the 1975 setting and the era of Eno's "albums", records that did more than just scratch the surface or float aimlessly, instead digging deep to reach new horizons, even when those horizons lay in unexpected places. Robert Wyatt handles percussion and Phil Manzanera plays differently, distorted, just as Eno sings differently: in a deep voice, enunciating deliberately, and slowing down his guitar, which seems to ooze as if made of fuel."Third Uncle" seems to begin with Roger Waters' bass, but Brian Turrington (who had previously played with Manzanera on Diamond Head) quickly launches into a tour de force, a race against time, while the Roxy Music guitarist does what he does best: transporting us from the known world to another dimension or universe, without spaceships or artificial substances, relying solely on the power of the mind and the act of listening. The composition was, of course, Eno's work; he adds weight to the notes and accelerates his vocal delivery, bordering on rapping, while the bass and guitar keep pace with his rapid-fire style, creating a true sonic experience. He would later elicit a similar approach from The Edge on U2's Zooropa, an album Eno was also involved in.The Portsmouth Sinfonia handles the strings on "Put A Straw Under Baby", a sound that is somewhat symphonic and childlike, yet also evokes a dockside atmosphere, with a deliberately nomadic feel. Vocal groups play a pivotal role on "Taking Tiger Mountain"; Randi & The Pyramids join Eno on "The True Wheel," creating a strange, postmodern pop-soul sound that even veers into punk and, thanks to Manzanera, experimental territory."China My China," once again featuring Robert Wyatt, sets out to subvert standard time signatures, incorporating atonal guitar work and the sounds of typewriters, alongside funky guitar lines.The title track closes the album; it is almost an elegy, one of those melancholic odes that are quintessentially Eno. Indeed, this is an album containing many Enos, and each distinct version faithfully represents the original. Yet there is no single original; there are many. There is the Krautrock Eno, the Fusion Eno, the Psychedelic, the Electronic, the Art-focused, and the Simple Eno, the latter being the persona he always chooses for his farewells, promising to return with a soul chorus that touches the very soul.
items._genre: progressive electronic / art pop / experimental / krautrock-influenced
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年发行的专辑延续了Eno对声音层叠与结构解构的探索，通过重复的调式纹理构建出类似中国套盒式的嵌套结构。专辑采用串行式生产理念，揭示音乐表象之下的多重含义，冷静的人声与变形的吉他各自承担不同的叙事功能，形成沃霍尔式的影像叠层。曲目横跨多个方向：从对六十年代迷幻流行（如Pink Floyd）的致敬，到更接近Krautrock的冷峻未来感；从Phil Collins将鼓转化为旋律乐器的实验合作，到Robert Wyatt参与的幽暗曲目。Andy Mackay的萨克斯被电子效果处理后模拟管乐器质感，甚至预示了Eno九十年代作品中的手法。Phil Manzanera的吉他与Brian Turrington的低音在不同轨道中以被拉伸的方式存在，节奏被持续打断与重构。整张专辑在流行可听性与实验性之间寻找张力，每首曲目都不是表面所呈现的样子。

items.body: Palagoma is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. Odd Okoddo, the duo of Kacirek and Ratengo, has been performing since 2018, but with the inclusion of the 83 year old Nengo, a singer from the eastern part of the country, there�s an added traditional depth to the music. A 2025 performance shows Nengo�s lifetime of experience singing Kenya�s dodo tradition around 2 and half minutes in (see below). Furthermore, her inclusion on this album allows her and Ratengo to toss the vocals back and forth as they reference their shared roots (Ratengo and Nengo live minutes from each other). Musically, however, the tracks are driven by Kacirek�s Buchla synth, hand percussion, and occasional kit drumming, which serve to buoy the voices without blotting out the music�s origins. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Bara,� for example, begins with the dime-store thwack of a repeated pattern, a stiff juxtaposition to the voices; yet, as the song rolls along, a 4/4 clink appears, then a burbling bass, and finally, what sounds like a xylophone. Layers of synthesized polyrhythms keep presenting themselves with a subtlety almost unnoticeable, until, by the track�s end, it feels organic, as if it�s all been underneath the two voices all along. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Sarah,� perhaps the album�s most intense track, features a lead vocal from Ratengo and tentative, percussive spittles from Kacirek. And while the technology never tries to overtake the vocals, it does sneak up and punctuate the track�s urgency, as edgy distortion sneaks in here and there just as Ratengo�s voice reaches its peak. The term �folktronica� has been bandied about as a way to house the type of music on offer here. In fact, exploratory collaborations such as Chouk Bwa & The �ngstr�mers as well as much of Kampala, Uganda�s Nyege Nyege label house sounds that might be �folktronic� in some way. What�s more interesting and important about this music, though, is how truly global so much of it is while maintaining a deep connection to Africa and its diasporic communities. The music on Palagoma , as well as much of what�s linked above (and available in countless other recent recordings) demonstrates a real willingness for cultures to respond to each other without trampling traditions altogether. Instead, roots become avant-garde and innovations become seemingly thousands of years old. Certainly the inclusion of an 83 year old traditional Kenyan singer only recently making her global debut as she tours with a duo whose instrumental voice is a white male saturated in electronic Kenyan rhythms demonstrates this blurring. The music this trio makes is certainly of the 21st century, but it�s often hazy, sparse, and open, keeping it from a quick sell-by date or confining it to a specific genre. Instead, it�s a beautiful example music as grace.
items.label: Cool Waters
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是内罗毕新厂牌Cool Waters的首发作品，由德国出生、驻肯尼亚的打击乐手Sven Kacirek与Olith Ratengo组成的二人组Odd Okoddo，邀来83岁东肯尼亚传统dodo唱法歌手Ogoya Nengo共同录制。Kacirek以Buchla合成器、手掌打击乐与套鼓为声音基底，人声在其间自由穿梭而不被淹没。《Bara》以反复的打击节奏起势，合成器多层次复节奏逐层叠加，最终与两条人声融为一体。《Sarah》则以Ratengo主唱，Kacirek的颗粒化打击与尖锐失真在声线高潮处悄然刺入。专辑的核心在于不同文化之间的真诚对话——欧洲电子语汇与东非传统歌唱在83岁老人的全球首演中相互回应，传统成为前卫，创新获得千年纵深。

items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: Dorothy Moskowitz 与 United States of Alchemy 项目于 2023 年带来专辑《Songs of Compassion》，由先锋作曲家 Francesco Paolo Paladino 与诗人 Luca Chino Ferrari 合作完成。整张专辑以钢琴为核心，辅以弦乐、木管、合成器音色层与金属质感音效，构建出非线性、非调性的听觉空间，刻意打破西方听众对和声进行的固有认知。歌词层面延续 1960 年代抗议歌曲传统，既直面当代政治议题，也探讨死亡与人类在宇宙中的位置。Moskowitz 的演唱不拘泥于旋律线条，而是让每个词获得自身重量，钢琴则充当另一重声部与评论者角色。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 的第二张专辑延续首作的杂糅风格，核心亮点在于全部乐器均由废旧物品手工制作——tassofons、tilofons、kitchenofon 等自造乐器在现代录音技术下依然保持了精准的音高与丰富的音质。乐队将自造乐器与音乐风格高度匹配：克莱兹默片段配以笑声单簧管与巴松，快速双拍打击乐营造狂欢感；昆比亚风格中长笛与西班牙语合唱交织，拉丁打击乐层次饱满；非洲节拍段落以木鱼、沙锤与响铃构建律动，玛林巴琴主奏搭配即兴炫技；中东旋律线则带有六十年代间谍剧配乐的恍惚气质。整张专辑以幽默态度回应了世界音乐的多样传统，同时通过字面意义上的'垃圾'乐器提醒人们：音乐的创造力不依赖昂贵器材，乐手总能找到发声的方式。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: Camilla Hole Trio 的新专辑延续了上一作将科幻合成器音色与传统挪威民间素材结合的探索路径，但整体风格更加落地。Hole 的主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，爵士影响显著。三人组的角色分配从不固定，开篇曲目《Springleik》以西挪威传统舞曲旋律为蓝本，Hole 先以萨克斯主奏旋律，Kalman 的模块合成器与 Nesheim 的颤音琴叠加增加色彩，随后 Kalman 拿起贝斯与 Hole 以齐奏方式重塑旋律线条，Nesheim 则进一步展开节奏维度。整首作品展现出强烈的即兴气质，旋律在即兴展开中不断回归。作为来自挪威的小众独立厂牌发行物，专辑将北欧民间音乐与自由爵士即兴、模块合成器声响实验融为一体，是兼具地域文化深度与跨界实验精神的代表作品。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — Fruupp, for years lived under the shadows of giants, as an opening act for bands like Genesis orKing Crimson, working hard to get recognition, the quintet was prolific in every sense of the word,and despite never getting any commercial success, some of their influence can be felt on genres suchas math rock or symphonic prog.Before the actual review starts, I'd like to take a moment to do something I am not acostumed to inthis site, I'd like to give the band some extra points for their wonderful sleeve art, which is aninteresting mix of medieval, impressionist and dadaist styles...unlike many eclectic covers whichare absurd for the sake for absurdity itself, this cover is absurd but also hides intention andartistic quality, anyone dedicated enough to aesthetics will get what I mean. It's a beautifulsleeve indeed.Starting off with that which is the absolute strength of this record : It's creativity and uniqueapproach. Northern Ireland had been a colony under British imperial rule for quite a while at thatpoint, so it's natural that aspects of cultural syncretism are to be felt across the 39 minutes ofmusic this album has, yet, it keeps most of the Irish musical identity intact, this is an act ofcultural resistance, but mixed with a proper dose of syncretism, it feels innovative, if they hadgone a little more British, then it would have hit the uncanny valley, yet this is not the case. Iwas quite surprised to learn that this band is not Iberian either, since strangely enough some ofthe modes, scales and rhythmic patterns are borrowed from Iberian music, this adds to a refreshingMediterranean sound mixed with strong Celtic influence, it's white funny how well these two stylesfit together in the record, since it *shouldn't* be that way as their almost opposite philosophiesin the way they approach this art. I also noticed some faint Arabic influences, but they are smalland barely noticeable, it's on tracks such as "Graveyard Epistle" where it can truly be felt...butit might as well just be the Iberian influence I mentioned before, since iberia is stronglyinfluenced by the Arab world due go the 700 years it spent under Arabic rule.The quality of the compositions is rich and diverse, despite being relatively short (between the 4and 8 minutes mark), they have several small movements, leitmotifs and variations, it's rhythmicallydense and that's it's clearest identity factor, across the record, the intricate and delicatepercussions, bass lines and guitars are condensed in a dance and struggle against each other,pushing to their limits and then coming together in complex polyrhythms, metrics and lines thatsyncopate and then go into chaos, over and over, it's hypnotic! The track "Song for a thought" is agreat example of this, it also incorporates classic Rock and roll elements. Then comes theambientation, oboes, string ensembles, delayed and reversed guitars and some clicking cymbals createan ambience of immersion and psychedelia which is ethereal in nature, it induces a high state ofconcentration and doesn't contradict the complex rhythms, if anything it complements them.If I had to describe the sound of this record in a single sentence it'd be : Baroque andmulticultural, vanguardist yet hypnotic...feels fresh even in 2026, which is 50+ years since it'srelease.The musicianship is great, and there's a natural chemistry between them all that holds thecompositions together like a glue, they are technically prominent (although not gifted) and have agreat sense of melody and rhythm, their teamwork is astonishing, specially the lead singers voicewhich is similar to Lake from ELP and Shulman from gentle giant. The production is okay, it doesfeel rough and noisy at times but putting this into context (underground act mainly known by collegestudents in Britain) it's understandable, it's something you can distract from if you will, andprobably will do so anyways because of how hypnotic this all is.Fans of gentle giant will love this since it feels a lot like "Acquiring the taste" (specially theslower, violin driven parts), the similarities are astounding, the band had not yet reached theirfull identity yet, but it's enjoyable anyways.A solid 5/5!
items._genre: symphonic prog / Celtic folk fusion / world music / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 北爱尔兰五人乐队 Fruupp 在1973年发行的专辑展现出丰富的文化融合特质，将凯尔特音乐根基与伊比利亚音阶节奏、隐约的阿拉伯元素交织在一起，形成独特的地中海与凯尔特混合色彩。评论着重指出专辑的节奏密度是核心标识：吉他、贝斯与打击乐在复杂的多节拍与切分结构中相互对抗又彼此缠绕，构成催眠式的律动张力。编曲虽然时长控制在四到八分钟之间，却包含多个小段落、主题动机与变奏，融合摇滚元素、双簧管、弦乐合奏与延迟反向处理吉他，营造沉浸式迷幻氛围。封面艺术融合中世纪、印象派与达达主义风格，被评价为兼具荒诞感与艺术意图。整体呈现出艺术抵抗与文化交融的双重特质。
