items.body: A pair of heavy hitting body music tours set to make their way across North America this fall ended up booking shows in Vancouver on the same day, and thankfully have been folded into one supercard, meaning that in a couple of months we’ll be getting to see Spike Hellis, Normal Bias, Buzz Kull, and Kontravoid all on the same night. A complete murderer’s row of modern EBM to be sure, but if you’re in NA you’ll likely have a chance to check out one if not both component parts as they’re extensive tours covering most of the continent. Hell, Spike Hellis is already on the road in support of the killer LP which finally dropped last week. Check the dates and grab tickets while listening to this week’s tracks. Are you Knormalled enough? Soft Vein, “Another Summer” Did you listen to our interview with Soft Vein on the podcast last week? If not, you should go do that right now, then come back here and listen to the exceptional “Another Summer”, yet another absolute stunner from the forthcoming All We’ve Known of Heaven. Justin Chamberlain’s songwriting, intimate style of performance and instrumentation keeps getting more undeniable with each release, and given the massive leaps he’s made in a mere three years, the overcast but beautiful skies are the limit for this melancholic LA based artist. One of our most hotly anticipated albums this year. All We've Known of Heaven by Soft Vein Patriarchy, “Bite Marks” Patriarchy are the enfants terrible of modern American darkwave, an act that provokes on stage and on record with each release. The thing is, the material backs it up, with last year’s excellent Manual For Dying showing off just how good the LA trio fronted by Actually Huizenga has gotten at bringing their gnarly stage show to their records. New EP Appendices is no different, featuring five tracks of mechanized shock rock and electro, expect to hear “Bite Marks” on your stompier dancefloors soonish. Appendices by Patriarchy Caustic, “Not Going Anywhere (Klack mix)” North American cult industrial impresario Matt Fanale follows up his last double LP Fiend with a remix album Unfiended, featuring a diverse roster of collaborators including Male Tears, Petrol Bastard, Alien Faktor, and Mark Pistel (!!!) amongst others. Of course Matt’s other project Klack dips in, bringing some of that new beat NRG to “Not Going Anywhere”, resolutely funky and full of more orch hits than a synclavier sample library. Giddy up! UNFIENDED by Caustic ner.ogris, “A View” German acts ner.ogris (or ner\ogris) have won us over via one LP and one EP of rock-solid electro-industrial which opts for considered grooves and sculpted sound design rather than shock or excess. This brooding taster from forthcoming LP Femme Fatale gets their strengths over quickly and artfully and bodes well for another course of proper home cooking from the pair. FAME FATALE by ner.ogris Knormalled, “The Servitor” The second EP from Indianapolis producer Knormalled shows a canny knack for a moody hybrid of dark electro and EBM which puts a premium on mood and slowly sliding timbral colour. Thru might best be appreciated as a full EP listen, but you can get a decent sense of the vibes from this shuddering slice. Should likely appeal if you’ve dug recent records by Kurs, or are still burning a candle for Distorted Memory. KNORMALLED THRU by Knormalled Ikon, “The Witness Tree” Some nice and easy summer goth rock from the always understated Aussie masters Ikon. Somewhat confusingly previewed then withdrawn, “The Witness Tree” is the first new material from Chris McCarter & co. in a few years and is setting up a forthcoming singles collection covering the entirety of the McCarter helmed era of the band. B-side’s got some dreamy pep, too. The Witness Tree single by IKON The post Tracks: August 10th, 2026 appeared first on I Die: You Die.

items.body: Band: Nostalghia | Album: Departure | Genre: Progressive metal | Year: 2026 From: Mexico City, Mexico | Label: Independent For fans of: Opeth, Enslaved, Riverside Bandcamp Nostalghia is a one-man project helmed by Mexican multi-instrumentalist Alex Becerra. This album is my first exposure to Nostalghia, but it looks like this is a very prolific project. According to RYM, this Departure is Nostalghia’s 14th release since their debut in 2020. The music on this record is stunningly diverse and ambitious. Aside from the band’s black metal roots, jazz, classical, alt-rock, classic prog, and more all play important parts here. “Leaving” opens the album on a restrained note. Acoustic guitar lines weave around one another in a way that draws from Baroque composers. When the vocals enter, they’re restrained. Rattling percussion, anxious strings, and tinkling piano build a sense of claustrophobia before suddenly cutting out and giving way to a melodic, piano-led passage that flows directly into the more-immediately-impactful opening of “Dearly Departed”. Riverside and Enslaved are both obvious influences in this song, with rapid, wiry guitar runs and vocals that vacillate between soulful and harsh. Latin jazz emerges about midway through as a nice bit of contrast. Many acts attempting such an incorporation come off as hokey and ham-fisted, but Nostalghia’s composition feels coherent and thought-out. The opening of “Uróboros” features some chamber music influence alongside restrained proggy folk, akin to acts like Jordsjø or Änglagård. When metal eventually emerges, there’s a wonderful, blistering solo supported by rich string arrangements. This sort of metal-classical hybrid is a not-uncommon trope in the realm of prog, but few acts pull it off this well. “Qa Muqu”, sung in a Mayan language and directly adapted from the Popol Vuh, has a peppy, jazzy opening. Enslaved-flavored black metal propels this piece along, with brass and piano exclamation points throughout. During instrumental passages, jazz once more comes to the forefront, and time signatures and rhythms get wonky as hell. The transitions between heavy and gentle moments are often sudden, but it all feels earned. Somber piano opens “Wherever You Are”. This is a mellow piece overall that gives the listener some appreciated breathing room. Riverside, Porcupine Tree, and Dream Theater’s better slow songs are all clear influences on this piece. “The Abyss Whispered” jumps back into metal, and tinkling chimes give it a celestial, otherworldly feel. The arrangements of the different parts of this song are diverse and complex, with some parts leaning into harsh black metal and others utilizing dissonant modern classical music. The final song on the album is the 10-minute “Offret (including “Ashes upon Eden”, “By the Corpse of Earth” and “Mercy”)”. “Ashes upon Earth” is led by clean guitar and pulls in elements of classical and dark folk music. I especially get flashes of some of Agalloch’s mellower output here. As distortion builds, so does the sense of majesty, before suddenly cutting out in the transition to “By the Corpse of the Earth”. Muted, atonal strings pluck and plink awkwardly and hauntingly, like the score to a horror film. Rattling chains and distant piano add to the ambiance. In the hands of less-skilled composers, this movement could easily become grating, but Becerra sells the tension and the anxiety. The final movement, “Mercy”, leans heavily upon ethereal atmospherics, with angelic vocals lifting everything skyward. Departure is a moving piece of music that displays an impressive breadth and depth of musical knowledge and skill. The songs demonstrate complex and technical instrumental ability, while the structures manage to be both diverse and coherent. The fusion of jazz and classical feels impressively natural, and I know there is a ton to discover upon repeated listens. Score: 92/100
items._genre: progressive metal / avant-garde metal / jazz fusion / classical / world music
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由墨西哥城单人多乐器演奏家Alex Becerra创作，是他自2020年以来的第十四张发行。作品横跨前卫金属、黑金属、爵士、古典、巴洛克、另类摇滚和世界音乐等多种风格，野心极大且执行统一。开篇以巴洛克风格的原声吉他交织铺陈，随后的曲目在急速金属段落与拉丁爵士、即兴钢琴、弦乐编排之间频繁切换，融合了Enslaved式粗粝黑金属与Riverside式旋律化前卫摇滚的特质。亮点之一是"Qa Muqu"曲目，直接取材于玛雅经典《波波尔乌》并以玛雅语演唱，将爵士、铜管与黑金属交织。专辑结构以最后十分钟的组曲"Offret"收束，包含多个乐章。整体来看，作品在重型与轻盈、现代与古典、墨西哥本土文化与北欧前卫传统之间建立了具有说服力的桥梁。

items.body:
Seoul’s Uman Thurman & Yetsuby, aka Salamanda, meditate on the inner life of a basil plant with a delicately flavoured suite of pottering pulses and harmonised warmth in a fine tradition of Far Eastern ambient electronica that chimes with label mates at GMT and the likes of E Ruscha V or Woo.

“The album moves through a full day in the plant's life opening with ‘introduce my atom which is my favorite one’, an act of quiet self-declaration in morning light, before settling into the unhurried rhythmic pulse of ‘to to ki toki tok’- the drip of water, the tick of a clock, the slow beat of photosynthesis. ‘allez, pousse!’ - one of the standouts in this journey - carries the basil's gentle will to grow, to push, to tilt toward the sun, while ‘hungry snail’ captures a moment of creaturely encounter on the glass: an uninvited visitor, moving slowly, wanting. As the afternoon deepens, 'Basil's Ritual' traces the daily ceremony of light and warmth, repeated with calm devotion from root to leaf. Night falls across 'Basil's Dream', and in the stillness something like sleep arrives - the plant resting, imagining tomorrow's sun. The album closes with ‘the blue wine’, a final mysterious reverie in which the basil seems to contemplate its own fate, somewhere between acceptance and wonder.”
items._cn_summary: 首尔双人组Salamanda以一株罗勒植物的内在生命为线索，构思了一整日的时间叙事：从清晨静谧的自我宣言，到午后光合作用般缓慢流动的节奏脉冲，再到夜间入梦般的宁静沉思。专辑以精心配比的微弱脉冲与和声质感为基调，水滴声与时钟滴答被转化为节拍素材，旋律推进极为克制。整体风格延续远东环境电子脉络，与GMT、E Ruscha V等厂牌同�气质相契。概念化的曲目编排与细腻的声音层次使其超越常规氛围音乐范畴，展现出将自然观察转化为抽象听觉体验的独特视角。

items.body:
Dean Blunt’s totemic, genre-agnostic first ’Black Metal’ album is back in circulation on the heels of its killer 2nd volume, singing out a singular sort of mid-decade London blooz where his myriad circles run into one.

In 2014 ‘Black Metal’ arrived as Blunt’s 4th solo album in a string of quietly groundbreaking and guess-again solo recordings following the break-up of Hype Williams, his duo with Inga Copeland. It was an instant fave, raved about everywhere, and with the benefit of hindsight is arguably one of the past decade’s definitive highlights; a record symptomatic of the way staid generic borders were dissolving, expressing a lucid but woozy pathos that still feels timeless, yet very much of its flat-time, when the stream of musical history had pooled into the reservoir of the internet.

Returning to its slow baked charms years later ‘Black Metal’ has lost none of its allure, with a reflective stillness still belying its depths. Nimbly joining wipe clean presets and crisp licks of original instrumentation with vocals by Blunt and regular spar Joanne Robertson, their baker’s dozen tunes somehow consolidate aspects of everything from hip hop to chamber music, indie-pop to R&B with experimental wit and ohrwurming magick that places it among his most memorable and surprising records.

From the symphonic Americana lilt of ‘Lush’ to its amazing 13 minute centrepiece of chamber soul gauze ‘Forever’ and the free jazz meets folk and roadrap synthscape of ‘Grade’ it coolly piques curiosity and perplexes from every angle, resolving unfamiliar styles with a pop-sharpened manner that follows a path first taken by A.R. Kane and which quite possibly ignited a reappraisal of the problematic way in which Black music has been perceived and categorised in popular/critical culture.

All time business = unmissable.
items._genre: experimental pop / lo-fi / chamber soul / hip-hop fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dean Blunt在2014年发行的第四张个人专辑，将嘻哈、室内乐、独立流行、R&B、民间音乐与自由爵士等多种元素融合在松散的低保真框架中。评论指出它打破了传统流派边界，体现了2010年代中期伦敦音乐场景中各类圈子交汇的独特状态。专辑以缓慢烘焙的质感、清晰的器乐片段与预设音色结合，配合Blunt与Joanne Robertson的人声，呈现一种迷幻而清醒的感伤特质。从'Lush'的美式交响民谣韵味，到长达13分钟的室内灵魂乐氛围曲'Forever'，再到融合自由爵士、民间与道路说唱的'Grade'，每首作品都以流行感性的方式调和陌生风格，被视为重新审视黑人音乐在流行文化中被认知与归类方式的起点之一。

items.body:
Avon’s lesser-hailed, glam ‘80s synth-pop and new wave movement is spotlighted in-depth via 20 songs compiled by studio engineer Dave Massey, who smartly portrays the breadth and quality of an ‘80s blindspot.

‘The Bristol & Bath Blitz Club Meets Art School Sound - 80's Explosion’ traces the reverberating influence of Rusty Egan and co.’s new wave crucible, The Blitz Club, along the M4 leyline, where it met Avon art school kids advancing from punk and funk into a new decade. Egan’s signature DJ brew - e.g. Kraftwerk to Visage, Burundi Black to Bowie, Japan and Grace Jones - would spark myriad emulators who were also mirroring the chops of Duran Duran (sons of the Brum club scene an hour north) and the likes of Martyn Ware et al in Sheffield, in their blends of US funk, European machine music, and a punky license to follow their nose. 

Fair to say it’s not the usual tale of Bristol’s dub-rooted and punk heritage. Between Distant Cousins’ Arabic-inflected new wave ace ‘Red Oasis’, and the angular chops of ‘Your Heart My Ambition’ from Frame By Frame, it checks for a spectrum of pop moxie taking in the swooning goth pop of Great Naked; BEF-meets-Bowie pomp of Wadi Vision; Nite Watch and glaxobabies’ disco-boogie; a stranger standout of synth sleaze by Startled Insects; Duran Duran-esque new wave funk by Creature Beat; and a ballad pearl by The Escape - all sure to mess with preconceptions of Bristol history.
items._genre: synth-pop / new wave / post-punk / goth pop / boogie
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦八十年代英国雅芳郡（Avon）布里斯托与巴斯地区被忽视的华丽合成器流行与新浪潮场景，由录音师Dave Massey精选二十首曲目，系统梳理了一条从The Blitz Club出发、沿M4走廊向西部延伸的地下脉络。合辑呈现了Bowie、Visage、Japan等新浪漫标杆对地方乐队的辐射效应，同时捕捉了杜兰杜兰式放克新浪潮、阿拉伯风新曲、哥特流行等多重面向。收录曲目跨越Disco Boogie到Synth Sleaze、从合成器华丽摇滚到深情慢歌，拼贴出与布里斯托通常被强调的dub根源与朋克脉络截然不同的另一面，挑战既有历史叙事，为英国八十年代地方音乐版图补上一块缺失拼图。

items.body:
jason calhoun’s fifth release for Dear Life Records,

"On revelations of divine love Calhoun has assembled an especially potent album of work that whirrs, hums, and glows. Unlike his recent output centered around extended, hypnotic compositions, the fourteen tracks here immediately request your attention and curiosity. Their concision only underscores one of his greatest strengths: the ability to capture an evaporating, fleeting moment, and hold it close.

The title is a nod to British Anchoress Julian of Norwich, whose collected writing of the same title is the earliest of any woman written in English. Here it serves as a unifying theme for Calhoun's particular palette of restless textures and tentative melodies. This is personal music, to be sure, but it also feels tactile, almost taffy-like in its presentation—and with such a potent combination, it is hard to resist a smile while listening. Like when the insistent pulse grounding 'last one' suddenly changes color as yawning tones reveal themselves, or how 'eye dilation' tiptoes into the room with each note sounding like a carefully chosen step. Though never precious or fussy, the album remains resolutely intimate.

Calhoun puts it plainly: “Julian of Norwich says “‘All shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well’. These days, I’ve been having my doubts that this is true. As no solution to the issue at hand, I look for the revelations of divine love in my life, and I find them--in my partner asleep on the floor in our studio, my survival of a social interaction with a stranger, being bad at chess. Don't ask me what they mean-I'm still figuring that out myself. Maybe we can figure it out together.” It is from this place of doubt, searching, and openness that the album finds its footing."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以中世纪英国女隐士朱利安·诺里奇的同名著作为概念框架，收录了十四首短小作品。Calhoun擅长捕捉转瞬即逝的细微声响，将不安分的质感纹理与试探性的旋律结合在一起，形成一种类似太妃糖般可触碰的音乐质地。专辑中的作品如'last one'通过音色色彩的突变展现层次变化，'eye dilation'则以小心翼翼的步伐营造出进入房间的氛围。整体呈现出私密、亲密的聆听体验，从怀疑与寻找的状态出发，将日常生活中的微小启示转化为声音。Dear Life Records作为独立厂牌为发行提供了合适的土壤，Calhoun此次有意偏离以往催眠式长篇结构，转向更为凝练的表达方式，展现了他对瞬间的把握能力。

items.body:
TTT tack to classical chamber music with the intimately fuzzy recital of richly melodic works written between mid-14th and 21st centuries and performed by NYC’s Cop Tears, a trio of early and avant garde music specialists; Derek Baron, Cameron kapoor, and John Andrew Wilhite.

Attending to an emergent TTT touchstone of recent times - as in Jack Sheen’s works, thru aspects of Will Bankhead’s What We and Guild mixes - Cop Tears lean into interests in quieter chamber music laced with threads of lo-fi, folk and jazz that tie ‘The Rules of the Game’ to the label’s key corpus. The 13 pieces follow five years from the trio’s ‘Theodor Adorno: Piano Works’, and five again from their debut ‘Thirteen Harmonies (1986) Selections From John Cage’s ‘Apartment House 1776’’, with enchanting slants on cherry picked pieces that endure, some over 600 years later, on the strength of their timeless arrangements.

In key with the label's thing, everything is swaddled in ferric gauze - possibly posited on auld tape recorders - and holds a peculiar, homely, discordant charm (including fits of giggles and room noise) for the duration, which never tests the patience. The C.14th, polyphonic chanson Ars Nova masterpiece of Guillaume de Machaut ‘Puis qu’en oubli’ is the set’s oldest, along with ‘Quam pulchra est’, a mid-C.15th work for recorder trio by John Dunstable, placed on the same page with the more angular chamber jazz modernism of ‘Selections from Piano Sonata after a Conversation with Jonathan Gean (2016)’ and their take on the naïf wooze of ‘Children's Music, No. 1, II: Modern Dance (1973)’ by Valentin Silvestrov. Our percy is the dreamy, creaking baroque elegance of ’S’io men vo (1618)’, but it’s best advised to take it all in one at your leisure...
items._genre: contemporary classical / chamber music / lo-fi / avant-garde / medieval
items._cn_summary: 纽约三人组合Cop Tears的成员均为早期音乐与先锋音乐专家，专辑选取从14世纪到21世纪的十三首曲目重新演绎，涵盖Guillaume de Machaut的中世纪新艺术复调 chanson、John Dunstable的15世纪牧歌、Valentin Silvestrov的现代钢琴小品以及多首当代作曲家的室内乐作品。所有演奏被模拟磁带质感的录音介质包裹，带有嗞嗞声、空间噪音甚至偶发的笑声，形成温暖而略显失谐的质感。这些改编并不追求学术化的原貌复原，而是以低保真、民谣与爵士触觉渗入早期音乐文本，使跨越数百年的旋律以当代卧室音乐的方式重新获得体温。整体编排跨度极大但情绪连贯，适合整张不间断聆听。

items.body:
Konx-om-Pax plays to his love of Brum/Detroit/Berlin techno and bittersweet braindance on his label, Display Copy

Tom Scholefield’s project typically folds in aspects of his background as animator and graphic designer into the highly visual auditory synaesthetics of the ‘Naja Naja EP’. On the title tune he deftly unfolds monotone Brum techno and the steely drive of Claude Young or Mills bangers into a tearing chromatic rager, whereas ’Tarantula’ listens u a lot with its ribboning lead reminding of Clark on a garage-techno tip, and ‘Phantasmal’ spirals the arps to a bittersweet braindance pinnacle.
items._cn_summary: Konx-om-Pax（Tom Scholefield）的《Naja Naja EP》延续了他对伯明翰、底特律与柏林techno的热爱，同时融入bittersweet braindance的抒情质感。作为动画师与平面设计师出身，他将视觉化的感知方式带入音乐创作：标题曲将单调的伯明翰techno节奏与Claude Young或Jeff Mills式的钢铁律动展开，演变为撕裂的色彩化狂暴；《Tarantula》以丝带般的领奏旋律漂浮，兼具garage-techno的律动与Clark式的感性；《Phantasmal》则将琶音盘旋至bittersweet braindance的高点。三首作品在techno骨架上各自展开不同的情绪面向，展现了严谨的结构感与鲜明的个人美学，发行于自家小厂牌Display Copy，整体保持地下与实验的独立气质。

items.body: Label: UnderPool, 2026 Personnel - Anggie Obin: flute; Bill McHenry: tenor saxophone; Miguel “Wiwi” Garcia: piano; Masa Kamaguchi: double bass; Estefania Chamorro: drums. Rising Panamanian jazz flutist and composer Anggie Obin, who attended Berklee College of Music in Boston and is based in Barcelona, gathers a first-class quintet—American saxophonist Bill McHenry, Cuban pianist Miguel “Wiwi” Garcia, Japanese bassist Masa Kamaguchi, and Spanish drummer Estefania Chamorro—for a wonderful debut album that honors her musical mentors and her late great-grandmother. Luz was titled after the latter, an important pillar in her life. “ For Mr. G ” begins the album in warm modal complicity, with saxophone and flute beautifully interlocking through contrasting timbres. The piece, dedicated to saxophonist Carlos Garnett—with whom Obin first recorded professionally—features her wandering freely, choosing exquisite, breathy notes with spotless intonation that makes us search as much as she does. There’s also catchy melodic input from McHenry, who captures Coltranean vibes in his solo, while Kamaguchi showcases the foundational sophistication for which he is known. “ Flash of the Spirit ”, a grateful nod to versatile bassist Santi Debriano, evolves with playful hard-bop flair, bluesy chops, and hints of Monk’s music. The quintet swings and grooves, revolving around freshly introduced ideas and a modern jargon that still drinks from the wells of tradition. Here, Obin is highly conversational in her statement, sounding as radiant as she does on “ Luz ”, where a delicate rubato introduction takes an emotional turn into a charming 3/4 drive. Obin’s expression is remarkable, Garcia’s measured piano playing comes wrapped in modal alchemy, while McHenry navigates abstract alleys of his own imagining. “ La Eucaristia ” exudes solemnity and dark contours through its leaping angular melodies, featuring an exchange of rapid motifs between Obin and McHenry. If the that piece was inspired by experimental multi-instrumentalist Anthony Braxton’s work, then the mercurial “ Ballot or the Bullet ” is a blues inspired by human rights activist Malcolm X’s speech. Obin kills it with soulful tones and brilliant technique. Recorded live at Estival de Jazz d’Igualada in Spain, Luz emphasizes the elasticity and potential of each composition, leaving a lasting impact. Obin’s highly attuned quintet cuts through modal post-bop and Panamanian roots with superb fluidity, providing an immersive listening experience. Favorite Tracks: 01 - For Mr. G ► 02 - Flash of the Spirit ► 04 - Luz
items._genre: modal post-bop / jazz / world fusion / Panamanian roots
items._cn_summary: 巴拿马爵士长笛手Anggie Obin的首张专辑由五重奏阵容演绎，曲目分别献给已故曾祖母以及多位音乐导师。作品以调式后波普为骨架，融入硬波普摇摆与巴拿马本土音乐元素，长笛与萨克斯在音色交织中形成对话，钢琴提供调式和声支撑，低音线条扎实。专辑既有温暖的调式氛围（如《For Mr. G》《Luz》），也有阴郁棱角的实验段落（如《La Eucaristia》受Anthony Braxton启发），以及带有蓝调语汇与人权致敬意味的《Ballot or the Bullet》。整体录制于西班牙音乐节现场，强调了乐手之间的即兴弹性与文化根源的流动性，展现了横跨美洲、欧洲、亚洲乐手的多元对话。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Several changes had taken place since the debut of Dave Stewart's band; there was only one track featuring vocals by Peter Blegvad, and John Greaves was on bass. There is a greater presence of wind instruments, which slow down both the fast-paced guitar passages and the keyboard sections. At times, "The Bryden 2-Step (for Amphibians) Part 1" takes on a somewhat anthemic quality (like Freeway Jam, by Jeff Beck), while at other moments it becomes more playful and slightly distorted."The Collapso" continues in a rock vein, sharing common ground with U.K.; however, Dave Stewart's highly disruptive keyboard interventions form a strong trio with the bass and drums, joined by the guitar, creating an atonal atmosphere almost reminiscent of Gentle Giant, before revisiting the same melody with a shift in pitch and rhythm. 'The Collapso' becomes an essay of multiple variations on the same melody, yet always distinct.Squarer for Maud, featuring cello and oboe, occupies another dimension entirely; yet other Stewart-led bands also updated their sound in 1978, such as Egg, with far more complex pieces by Phil Miller that take on a dramatic quality thanks to the organ backing. The oboe plays free jazz, accompanied by the rest of the band at a frenetic pace, until the piano stands alone like an island amidst Peter Blegvad's spoken-word delivery, a moment of calm before Phil Miller's return. With a string section that could belong on an Art Zoyd album.Of Queues and Cures is definitely their most rock-oriented album, yet it is well-balanced with the Canterbury essence and a style featuring wild, distorted keyboards sharing the spotlight with the guitar on "Dreams Wide Awake", a track that feels like an endless jam session, yet contains a melody full of groove and emotion at its core. On "Binoculars," John Greaves sings, his effective deep voice tracing the sinuous melodies laid out by his bandmates, while Jimmy Hastings' flute offers a most welcome, sweet gift, adding sonic variety; the display case on the album cover, with its jars full of mysteries, recalls the school library that Malcolm McDowell and his friends stormed in Lindsay Anderson's 1968 film If.... Ten years later, Dave Stewart would storm listeners' ears, using trumpets and trombones to craft a melody that snapped us out of any trivial monotony."Phl'kat'n" is another nod, somewhere between Zeuhl and Zappa, that allows "The Bryden 2-Step (for Amphibians) Part 2" to kick off with an avant-garde flair, a cutting-edge spirit that sweeps everything before it; John Greaves on bass and Dave Stewart on keyboards launch into a solid jazz-rock section before plunging into the depths, as the title suggests, and quietly fading away... because one doesn't need to make noise to go down in history.
items._cn_summary: 这是National Health的第二张专辑，也是乐队最具摇滚倾向的作品，同时保留了Canterbury场景的核心特质。乐队经历人事变动后，加入了贝斯手John Greaves，Peter Blegvad的人声仅在一首曲目中出现。管乐器分量加重，与吉他和键盘形成层次丰富的对话。Dave Stewart的无调性键盘介入与贝斯、鼓构成张力极强的三重奏，接近Gentle Giant式的张力感。《Collapso》围绕同一旋律展开多重变奏，每段都各有面貌。《Squarer for Maud》以大提琴与双簧管营造另类维度，双簧管自由爵士化的演奏与钢琴独白形成戏剧性对比。《Dreams Wide Awake》呈现狂野失真键盘与吉他的即兴对话。《Binoculars》中Jimmy Hastings的长笛音色甜美，与Greaves低沉嗓音的蜿蜒旋律互补。《Phl'kat'n》在Zeuhl与Zappa之间找到平衡点，为专辑注入前卫实验气息。整体编曲层次繁复，结构开放，是Canterbury场景中融合爵士摇滚与前卫实验的代表作。

items.body: Une Vraie Gothique – literally translated as A True Goth – is a French duo that came into existence in Paris in 2023, founded by Ulrika and Ferdinand Legendre. This year, Manic Depression Records released their debut album, “R.D.V. Au Cimetière”, an eclectic take on dark Electronic music where EBM, Dark-Wave and Techno collide. Their identity is every bit as important as their music: corpse paint, dark humor, French and German lyrics, and a generous wink towards the codes and clichés of Goth culture all come together to create a universe that is at once serious, absurd and irresistibly danceable. The album’s nine tracks take the listener on a journey into a world where darkness and absurdity go hand in hand. A defining element of the record is the interplay between the two voices: Ulrika sings in German, while Ferdinand delivers his vocals in French, making many of the tracks feel like a dark and intriguing dialogue. For me personally, this debut is an absolute revelation. A band whose name may initially sound like the ultimate Goth cliché – although I see it much more as a hilarious reference to the scene that clearly inspires them – manages to turn those very clichés on their head. The real strength and originality of Une Vraie Gothique lie in their compositions. They crack open the codes of different genres and reshape them into something distinctly their own, creating what feels much more like an ode to underground Electronic music than a parody of it. “R.D.V. Au Cimetière” is one of those albums I was instantly sold on. So, it is high time to get to know Ulrika and Ferdinand from Une Vraie Gothique a little better and discover what exactly lies behind the corpse paint, the French and German incantations, and that irresistible urge to meet somewhere in the cemetery… (Courtesy by Inferno Sound Diaries) MD176 – UNE VRAIE GOTHIQUE "R.D.V. au Cimetière" by Une Vraie Gothique Une Vraie Gothique interview Q: Could you tell us how you first met and how that eventually led to the creation of Une Vraie Gothique? Were there any particular artists or albums that served as important points of reference in shaping your sound? Ferdinand: We met at a mutual friend’s house, and Ulrika had asked me to help her compose an Electro-Disco track on the theme of the tiger for a performance she was doing at a Parisian cabinet of curiosities. Our conversations about music led us to realize our shared love of Goth music. So we decided to launch this project, starting with the title track, “Une Vraie Gothique.” We don’t really have any major points of reference, but I’d say we’re influenced by a huge number of different projects. For my part, Suicide Commando and Hocico immediately come to mind, for example. Ulrika: When that tiger project was finished, we had a sleepover where we were supposed to start working on a Euro-Dance track (one of our guilty pleasures). But instead, we watched “Hellraiser”, sampled ‘Demons to Some, Angels to Others’, (which you can hear at the beginning of our track “Une Vraie Gothique” ) and the process of becoming a true Goth was set in motion! I wish I could tell you another story and say that we probably connected in immaterial realms long before we met four years ago, but that’s still a topic under investigation. Q: I imagine the band’s name is meant to be taken with a touch of humor, but I’m still curious about the story behind it. Why did you choose Une Vraie Gothique, and if it does refer to Gothic culture, what does that scene and its music represent to you personally? Ulrika: We get asked a lot about this. Do I relate to the Goth scene and culture? Definitely. Come on, I was reading all classical Goth books, from Ann Radcliffe to Baudelaire, watching my classmates out of the corner of my eye in high school, while taking refuge in the school cloister to take black-and-white photos in long dresses. Do I see myself as a ‘genuine gothic’? Of course no. No one could… let’s then joke about it? In fact, I don’t think seriousness and humor are incompatible, except in Kundera’s “The Joke”, which deals with a totalitarian system. For me, the Goth scene is that undeniable feeling of being at home. I go down into a basement, drawn by the light and the sounds, by the promise of an intensity that’s both painful and joyful. Bodies dancing, minor scales. It’s already a contradiction in itself! The Goth scene is about celebrating life, with one foot in another world (the world of the dead, the world of shadows?). There’s a kind of haunting ritual, wrapped in a contemporary aesthetic. I wanna be a part of it, as a priestess. Ferdinand: Goth music represents my musical ‘family’. I discovered it through a sampler from Elegy magazine around 2003, and even though I developed my musical taste by listening to a wide variety of genres, it was Goth music that most gave me that sense of ‘belonging’ to a musical family. It was also at these parties that I danced the most and watched others dance. Among Goths, as in any social group, there are certain attitudes and recurring elements that you can have fun with while still respecting them. My friends and I have always had a great sense of self-deprecating humor, and we loved to laugh at ourselves. At first, we couldn’t quite come to terms with the fact that we were goths, even though we were clearly identified as such by everyone outside the movement who interacted with us. I think “Une Vraie Gothique” tells this story—the playful questioning of a genre’s identity that sometimes tells its followers, ‘If you want to be different, be like us’. In this project, we’re trying to strike the right balance: the band is perfectly accessible at face value (especially because of Ulrika’s character, who talks almost exclusively about personal things), but you can also have fun reading between the lines to uncover humorous elements. Q: Strictly speaking, your music doesn’t sound traditionally Gothic. Instead, it blends elements of EBM, Electro-Wave and even Techno, while it’s mainly the atmosphere and the song titles that evoke a Gothic aesthetic. How would you describe your musical identity, and how do you see the relationship between your Electronic sound and the themes explored in your lyrics? Ferdinand: Ulrika and I both listen to a huge variety of very different music. I’ve listened to a lot of Techno, actually, and quite a bit of Rap, which comes through in some of the tracks and in the way I use my voice at times. I think you’re right: the music itself isn’t necessarily ‘Goth’ in the traditional sense. It’s more of a reflection of a movement that has evolved and influenced many different musical styles. I feel like we’re living in an amazing era for music. Things are much less compartmentalized than before. There are Pop bands with a Goth aesthetic; Techno has become much darker; and many people in Hip-Hop don’t hesitate to rock leather and latex looks. We use elements that come from all over the place and that serve the purpose of the tracks: metal clangs, animal sounds, and a variety of synths and VSTs. We want our tracks to be hard-hitting and dark; we compose from the heart, and we’re our own biggest fans. Even if we wanted to make an entire album consisting solely of dark Electro tracks, I’m not sure we could pull it off. We’re diverse by nature. Ulrika: I like the opportunity to create my own music and follow my own, personal and unique vision. As I said in the previous question, I am definitely truly and completely related to the Goth/dark/alternative scene. BUT I want to be true to myself also, and I have to recognize different parts I am made of. To me, our musical identity is soft & sexy. The scent of Père Lachaise Cemetery on a windy day. Why? We often have a sultry bass line and pleasant, mellow mid-range frequencies. And I use my voice in a percussive, unsettling, incantatory way (the graves), whilst also allowing myself to incorporate more lyrical and mystical elements (the great wind). My influences are related to Germany: Deine Lakaien, Welle:Erdball, Helium Vola, Sopor Aeternus, Lacrimas Profundere, Agonoize, Feindflug, Nina Hagen, Bohren & Der Club Of Gore… as far as possible, I preferred to listen to German lyrics and, as I was in Metz in my childhood (East of France), it made more sense to look across the border. As for the Electronic aspect, I just want to say that I love powerful basslines and energetic kicks, paired with melodies you can really let loose to. In our lyrics, we’re always talking about connection and energy. ‘Electronics’ comes from ‘electron’. It’s what carries electricity. I feel like I’m right at the heart of my material theme! Q: How did the two of you collaborate on “R.D.V. Au Cimetière”? What roles does each of you take on within the creative process, and what were the biggest challenges you encountered during the writing, recording and production of the album? Ulrika: Thanks for this question. It’s great to talk about the creative process! For me, the biggest challenge is finding our signature style, our identity, our voice. We’re walking a tightrope between our influences and our own inner worlds. I’ve made huge progress writing this album by allowing myself to simplify and pare down musical phrases to give them more impact. I’d like to do that even more. We also try to focus on using variations rather than introducing new elements when we want the song to evolve. One of our favorite questions now is, ‘What if we did a bass variation?’. Right after ‘What filter should we put on the keyboard?’ Ferdinand: We’re both involved in every stage of the songwriting process. We both write and compose equally. Sometimes one of us needs to spend a few hours working on the song alone, and then we come back to it together, but overall we work as a team. Usually, I start by suggesting a rhythm and bassline, and Ulrika adds variations to it, then fairly quickly brings in vocal elements and a narrative direction. Sometimes we work together, and sometimes we take turns, but we always end up with a song to which we’ve both contributed equally. The biggest challenge was undoubtedly not going off in all directions. There were times when we took the humor too far, for example, and the song became way too parodic, so we had to completely backtrack. As mentioned earlier, our main challenge is finding the right balance between paying homage to that scene and allowing for different levels of interpretation.Q: You are based in Paris, which seems to have become an increasingly vibrant hub for both the Electronic and Gothic underground scenes. What is it like to be part of that environment? Does a city like Paris influence artists in a way comparable to cities such as Berlin, or does it have its own unique creative identity? Ferdinand: Paris is lucky to have so many ‘underground’ venues and an endless cultural heritage. The walls have a history, and there are so many people that you always end up meeting others who are interested in what you’re offering and who understand your vision. We also have a vibrant cultural scene in the suburbs—I’m thinking of cities like Montreuil, for example, which have always been very open to alternative ideas. I don’t know if our city influences us the way Berlin might, but it certainly offers us plenty of opportunities to connect with others. Ulrika : I find inspiration in old places. I love cemeteries, and coming across churches, works of art, and objects from the 12th century is definitely a source of enchantment. I studied at the school of the Louvre, which had a profound impact on me. That’s why I chose to live in Paris. Besides, it’s the only city I know where I can go to a medieval music concert of Hildegard von Bingen or Perrotin on Monday, a Black-Metal show on Tuesday, a math lecture on Wednesday, an Electro-Goth show on Thursday, and a batcave show on Friday. We’re incredibly lucky to be surrounded by this beautiful heritage, and I want to honor and share it. I feel enriched by this multicultural history of dark music from today and yesterday, sometimes looking back several centuries ! Q: Have you already started working on new Une Vraie Gothique material or other projects? Looking back at “R.D.V. Au Cimetière”, how critical are you of the album today? Are there aspects you’re particularly proud of, and are there things you would approach differently next time? Ulrika: We are currently working on a documentary that we filmed in February 2026 in California at the Mars College Festival. We had the immense pleasure of being invited by Vanessa Rosa and Gene Kogan to the desert to collaborate with the artists/developers and create a song about Euler’s Basel formula, in which we seek to convey the emotional impact of a theoretical argument. That’s my ultimate quest! We’re finishing up the composition of the song and wrapping up the editing! Is math Gothic? It’s full of formulas, after all. As for the album, this is my first release with this kind of project. There are inevitably things we’d like to take further, but I’m extremely proud of the work we’ve done, and I enjoy listening to the tracks without feeling like they’re mine. That’s a good sign! Moving forward, I’d like to simplify things even more, making them even more effective and precise. Asking myself, ‘What can we take away?’ rather than ‘What can we add?’ ‘Less is more’ (Mies van der Rohe) is a powerfull statement. Ferdinand: I’m very proud of this debut album; it really captures our work and the first narrative arc of Une Vraie Gothique. That said, I can’t wait to release new material, and we’re already working on the next album. In fact, we’re playing several songs live that aren’t on “R.D.V. Au Cimetière” but will be on the next one, such as “France Gothique” or the more recent “Anathème.” I think we’ve both grown in many ways; I don’t think there’s any aspect we’ll need to approach fundamentally differently next time. We’re going to keep putting out great songs and try to get our music out there at festivals and abroad. We’re also very happy with our first music video, “Nuée Ardente,” directed by Anaïs Novembre, which brings a welcome new visual dimension to the project.
items._cn_summary: 这是一支来自巴黎的二人组合，2023年成立，首张专辑由法国独立厂牌Manic Depression Records发行。专辑融合了EBM、Dark-Wave与Techno三种电子音乐脉络，九首曲目在阴郁的氛围中保持着强劲的舞曲节奏。最具辨识度的设计是双主唱的跨语言对话——女主唱使用德语演唱，男主唱则以法语呈现，形成一种诡异的对位感。尸妆、法德歌词交替、哥特亚文化的戏谑解构构成了乐队的视觉与文本策略，乐评人将其定位为对地下电子音乐的礼赞而非戏仿。音乐受到Suicide Commando与Hocico等工业电子先驱的影响，同时将Euro-Disco与Electro-Disco元素作为隐秘的趣味参照融入创作，在黑暗与荒诞之间建立了一种独特的美学平衡。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了圣多美和普林西比在1970至80年代录制的Puxa音乐，融合了葡语非洲殖民地传统节奏与加勒比海地区的merengue、Soukouss等元素。多把吉他相互交织盘旋，人声与旋律框架融为一体，鼓与吉他在低音和键盘让位时驱动舞者进入狂热状态。Pedro Lima带领的乐队展现了被压抑的吉他即兴与鼓手的激烈交锋，Sangazuza则以干练的节奏编排呈现厚重律动。专辑记录了这个非洲第二小国在缺乏城市录音工业背景下留下的稀有声学遗产，通过小厂牌Bongo Joe的发掘使其重新进入当代听众视野。整体而言，这是对边缘化音乐传统的珍贵抢救，具有独特的文化历史价值与跨地域节奏融合的趣味。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body: Tricky turns the difficult stuff into sound rather than sermon, and the result is an album that feels less like an elegy than a deeply lived affirmation of being here. No, not a return to form. The form was never abandoned. Instead, a deeply resonant expression of a singular experience eventually known finally by all. Alpha to Omega. A sonic symbol for the game of life Different When It's Silent by Tricky // False Idols   Actual legend Tricky has been on my radar since Massive Attack’s Blue Lines days, from “Karmacoma” and his forever-faultless first album Maxinquaye. I bought the digipack singles “Ponderosa” and “Aftermath,” and fell deeply for Alex Reece’s remix of “Brand New Retro.” To have his thirty-years-later work, Different When It’s Silent, on my figurative desk to write a commentary on is a foundationally humbling notion. Let’s be clear: there are no airs and graces about this new set of emotionally resonant tracks, and as a result, expect no airs and graces from this attempt to put into words a profoundly touched and cosmically imbibed album as Tricky presents here. From the outset there is a cornerstone of authenticity that I’m not sure Tricky could avoid for all the money in the world. If heart-on-the-sleeve were a creative pulse—and it often is, and if I had my way always would be—then this album, and its purveyor, Tricky, are the embodiment of that same intention. Even if a person were not an artist and were merely a voyeur of any form of art, authenticity would be the facet they would recognize without necessarily knowing they were in its presence. Authenticity is the key to reaching into the place within an audience member that an artist desires to touch: the artist channels the piece they are working ​on by paying attention to the creative pulse as it moves through them. That symmetry, that resonance, is beyond the control of artist and audience. But when it is channeled to the degree to which it is here, the creative piece simply appears. This notion should not undermine the capacity to pay attention to the creative whorl as it passes through the creator of the work. With the intent of a fractured but reassembled vase for life, Tricky neatly assembles, in simple terms, a group of local and distant cohorts, and a rudimentary application of post-rock, trip-hop beats, rhymes and loves for life—either here or there—forming perhaps the most cohesive fractured, broken and complete incompleteness: a sonic symbol for the game of life.   A neat hybridization of acoustic and sampled work :: Vocal duties are shared between Mitch Saunders’ beautiful falsetto, Run Red Rambo’s tight bars, Radana’s gravitas, False Idol’s own Marta Zlakowska, and Tricky himself. The musical palette is a neat hybridization of acoustic and sampled work. Throbbing bass pulses across tribal tom rhythms; atmospheres and tones are melancholic, adding to that same emotional heft. Moods move between optimism and broken-heartedness: crying to be seen and pleading to be heard wrestle alongside hope for the future and the feeling of being alive after retreating for an undisclosed time. After all, no one is immune to life, right? In places such as “Be Still in the Pain,” there is self-aware anger against loss and presence. On the frankly astounding “Piano,” choral laments parry against Mitch’s tender lament. “Marinade”—string quartet and Tricky’s vocal musing—paints a wonderful canvas for realness personified. And Marta’s appearance on closing track “Out of Place” is frankly stunning. In the end, it’s an open heart that opens the heart. It’s delightfully real. And Tricky’s paean to his daughter carries a weight that makes the whole record feel suddenly more human, more fragile. There is something profoundly moving in hearing someone arrive at that place where love, absence and mortality occupy the same space—where the knowledge that nothing and no one can be held onto forever becomes not an abstraction, but something lived and felt. Yet the album doesn’t dwell there. Instead, that awareness seems to feed back into the music itself: the warmth of the acoustic elements, the bruised electronics, the fractured rhythms, the choral textures and those beautifully human voices all become part of the same emotional vocabulary. Mortality is present, certainly, but so is life in all its messy, sensual, rhythmic immediacy. Tricky turns the difficult stuff into sound rather than sermon, and the result is an album that feels less like an elegy than a deeply lived affirmation of being here. No, not a return to form. The form was never abandoned. Instead, a deeply resonant expression of a singular experience eventually known finally by all. Alpha to Omega. Different When It’s Silent is available on False Idols. [Bandcamp] Different When It's Silent by Tricky // False Idols  The post Tricky :: Different When It’s Silent (False Idols) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Tricky多年创作脉络的延续，将trip-hop节拍与后摇滚质感相融合，以原声与采样并置的方式构建声响层次。贝斯脉冲在部落鼓点上游走，氛围低沉忧郁，情绪在乐观与心碎之间游移。人声部分由多位合作者分担——真假声交替的脆弱演绎、紧密的说唱歌词、沉稳的嗓音——共同丰富了整张专辑的人声纹理。评论指出，Tricky延续了他一贯的真实性表达，没有刻意的风格回归，而是以碎片重组的方式呈现生命的完整与残缺。作为False Idols厂牌出品，非大型商业厂牌。整体评论偏重情感与哲学层面的感悟，对音乐技法的拆解较为有限，但展现出创作者对协作与生活主题的沉稳把控。

items.body: Slovenian industrial group Laibach will give “Die Kanone”, its collaboration with Bijelo Dugme, a first physical release on October 30, 2026, via Matrix Music Arhiv (MMA), distributed through Audioglobe. The release comes on two vinyl editions and a digipak CD, and follows the digital-only single Laibach issued via Mute in July 2025. “Die Kanone” reworks “Top” (“The Cannon”), the first single Bijelo Dugme released in 1974, recast by Laibach in German for a collaboration initiated by Bijelo Dugme founder and songwriter Goran Bregović to mark that band’s 50th anniversary. The October 30 release adds the track’s Slovenian-language version, “S topom te bom ciljal moja mala” (“I’ll Aim My Cannon at You, My Little One”), together with previously unreleased remixes by German industrial and EBM act Die Krupps, UK producer the Lincolnshire Poacher, and Slovenian-Croatian electronic duo Black Dot. Both the German and Slovenian versions are being made available on a physical format for the first time. The vinyl LP is issued in a limited green edition and a standard black edition, both carrying the same six tracks: “Die Kanone”, “S topom te bom ciljal moja mala”, the Die Krupps remix, the Lincolnshire Poacher mix, the Black Dot version, and a live recording of “Die Kanone” performed with the RTV Slovenia Symphony Orchestra at the Ljubljana Opera. The CD, released as a digipak, carries all six tracks plus two exclusive bonus cuts not available on vinyl: a live version of “S topom te bom ciljal moja mala” recorded at the same Ljubljana Opera performance, and a karaoke version of “Die Kanone”. ‘Die Kanone’ tracklist across formats Vinyl LP (green and black editions): A1 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – 3:03 A2 “S topom te bom ciljal moja mala (I’ll Aim My Cannon at You, My Little One)” – 3:01 A3 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – Die Krupps remix – 3:41 B1 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – the Lincolnshire Poacher mix – 5:18 B2 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – Black Dot version – 4:34 B3 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – live at the Opera with RTV Slovenia Symphony Orchestra – 3:05 Digipak CD: 01 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – 3:03 02 “S topom te bom ciljal moja mala (I’ll Aim My Cannon at You, My Little One)” – 3:01 03 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – Die Krupps remix – 3:41 04 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – the Lincolnshire Poacher mix – 5:18 05 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – Black Dot version – 4:34 06 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – live at the Opera with RTV Slovenia Symphony Orchestra – 3:05 07 “S topom te bom ciljal moja mala (I’ll Aim My Cannon at You, My Little One)” – live at the Opera – 2:51 08 “Die Kanone (The Cannon)” – karaoke version – 2:52 About Laibach Laibach was formed in 1980 in Trbovlje, Slovenia, then part of Yugoslavia, by Dejan Knez, Milan Fras, Ervin Markošek and Ivan Novak. The group positioned itself from the outset as a multimedia collective, pairing martial industrial sound with provocative imagery, performance art and sociopolitical critique, and later became the musical wing of the Neue Slowenische Kunst art collective. After early cassette releases, Laibach’s debut album appeared on ŠKUC ROPOT in 1985. International attention followed a signing to Mute Records, which released “Opus Dei” in 1987, featuring reworkings of Queen’s “One Vision” and the Austrian national anthem “Geburt einer Nation”. Laibach has maintained a steady release pace since, with albums including “NATO” (1994), “Volk” (2006) and “Spectre” (2014), and has worked with symphonic ensembles and experimental artists on projects such as “Also sprach Zarathustra” and, more recently, “Alamut” with A/Political. In 2015, Laibach became the first Western band to perform in North Korea. The group’s 2026 studio album “Musick” was released via Mute earlier this year, following a 2026 European tour. The current lineup includes Milan Fras, Ivan Novak, Luka Jamnik and Rok Lopatič. Laibach initiated its collaboration with Bijelo Dugme – the Sarajevo rock band founded by Goran Bregović in 1974 whose original 1974 single “Top” is reworked on “Die Kanone” – at Bregović’s request, to mark Bijelo Dugme’s 50th anniversary. The two acts first released “Die Kanone” digitally via Mute and Classic Records in July 2025. The October 30, 2026 release on Matrix Music Arhiv brings the collaboration to vinyl and CD for the first time, adding the Slovenian-language version and three new remixes alongside a live recording made with the RTV Slovenia Symphony Orchestra at the Ljubljana Opera.
items._cn_summary: 斯洛文尼亚工业团体Laibach与波斯尼亚传奇摇滚乐队Bijelo Dugme合作，重新演绎后者1974年首支单曲《Top》，以德语版本《Die Kanone》呈现，并将作品交由Die Krupps、the Lincolnshire Poacher、Black Dot等不同风格的电子音乐人重新混音。十月底发行的实体版本包含黑胶与Digipak CD两种载体，曲目编排兼顾原始德语与斯洛文尼亚语版本，以及与卢布尔雅那歌剧院RTV斯洛文尼亚交响乐团合作的现场录音。整体企划跨越工业电子、欧陆摇滚与古典管弦乐编制，融合巴尔干音乐根源与中欧工业美学，为Bijelo Dugme五十周年纪念提供了具有仪式感的跨语境再诠释。

items.body: Stephan Groth, founder and vocalist of Apoptygma Berzerk, turns 55 on August 10, 2026. The Norwegian EBM and synthpop act, which Groth has led since 1989, marks the birthday alongside “Kathy’s Song XXV,” a 25th-anniversary reissue campaign built around one of the band’s best-known tracks, “Kathy’s Song (Come Lie Next to Me).” Groth was born on August 10, 1971, in Odense, Denmark, and relocated with his family to Sarpsborg, Norway, in 1986. He founded Apoptygma Berzerk in 1989 together with Jon Erik Martinsen, taking the band’s name from a word picked at random out of a dictionary, derived from the Ancient Greek for “piece of a tunic.” Martinsen left the group early on, and Groth has remained its sole constant member and main songwriter since. The band’s first two albums, “Soli Deo Gloria” (1993) and “7” (1996), established a darker EBM and electropop sound. “Welcome to Earth” (2000) moved toward a lighter, more experimental style and included “Kathy’s Song (Come Lie Next to Me),” built around a vocoded chorus voiced by Kathy Macintosh. The single followed on December 11, 2000, with a remix from Ferry Corsten that became a trance-scene favorite and helped push the song beyond the EBM and futurepop audience. “Harmonizer” (2002) leaned further into synthpop, “You and Me Against the World” (2005) took the band toward an indie rock-oriented sound, “Rocket Science” followed in 2009, and “Exit Popularity Contest” (2016) returned to the band’s earlier electronic roots. Beyond Apoptygma Berzerk, Groth has recorded as H2O with Geir Bratland in the mid-1990s and is a member of Fairlight Children, a lighter, pop-oriented electronic project that issued a limited vinyl edition of its “808Bit” album in February 2025. 2026 has brought “Kathy’s Song (Come Lie Next to Me)” back into focus. The 25th-anniversary “Kathy’s Song XXV” edition arrived digitally in December 2025, first on Bandcamp and then across other platforms, with new remixes by Ferry Corsten – who reworked his original 2000 remix – alongside Per Martinsen (Mental Overdrive) and Alyxx Digre (Zone Tripper). Groth has said the track is “probably the most important song I have ever written,” and described the vocoded chorus, recorded with Fredrik Darum and Vegard Blomberg, as something that “had never been done before” at the time. A physical follow-up arrived via emmobiz with a limited vinyl reissue, released on July 10, 2026. Stephan Groth marks 55th birthday as Apoptygma Berzerk celebrates ‘Kathy’s Song’ anniversary The overlap of Groth’s 55th birthday with the ongoing “Kathy’s Song” anniversary campaign places two Apoptygma Berzerk milestones in the same year. Side-Line previously covered the band’s 25th anniversary of “Soli Deo Gloria” with the “SDGXXV” reissue project in 2018, a similar reworking of an early album that Groth has cited as a direct model for how the “Kathy’s Song XXV” campaign was organized. About Apoptygma Berzerk Apoptygma Berzerk was founded in Norway in 1989 by Stephan Groth and Jon Erik Martinsen. Martinsen departed soon after, leaving Groth as the band’s vocalist, programmer, guitarist and sole constant member. The band’s debut album, “Soli Deo Gloria,” was released in 1993 and established a dark EBM and electropop sound, followed by “7” in 1996. Geir Bratland joined on keyboards in 1995, having already worked with Groth on the ambient techno side project H2O in the mid-1990s. “Welcome to Earth” arrived in 2000, softening the band’s earlier darker themes and including “Kathy’s Song (Come Lie Next to Me),” with vocals by Kathy Macintosh and a single release that December featuring a Ferry Corsten remix. “Harmonizer” followed in 2002 in a more synthpop-oriented direction, and “You and Me Against the World” (2005) marked a more mainstream, indie rock-influenced turn for the band, a departure the group revisited with expanded reissues in 2021. “Rocket Science” was released in 2009, and “Exit Popularity Contest” (2016) returned to the band’s earlier electronic and EBM-rooted sound. Alongside Apoptygma Berzerk, Groth has recorded as H2O with Bratland and continues as a member of Fairlight Children, a lighter, pop-oriented electronic project. The band marked the 25th anniversary of “Soli Deo Gloria” with the “SDGXXV” reimagining released in 2018 and 2019, and has since applied the same approach to “Kathy’s Song,” releasing the “Kathy’s Song XXV” remix EP in December 2025 and a limited vinyl edition in July 2026. Stephan Groth turns 55 on August 10, 2026, with more than 35 years of Apoptygma Berzerk behind him and, by his own account, new material still in progress.

items.body:
Cathedral is a thrilling album and terrifying graphic novel from director and musician John Carpenter, based on a dream Carpenter had in 2024.

"An abandoned cathedral. A gruesome murder. A powerful supernatural entity living in the catacombs. It all comes to a head in downtown Los Angeles. What will happen and who will live to tell the tale? Such is the storyline of Cathedral, it has all the drama, dark atmosphere, and frenetic pacing of a classic heavy metal record. Especially designed as the soundtrack to the graphic novel, each track corresponds to a specific section of the book. The liner notes included with the album packaging feature prompts for each track, creating a fully interactive experience. Combined with the graphic novel, it’s the closest thing to a new John Carpenter film in years.

The music on Cathedral retains all the eerie atmosphere and sinister propulsion of the epochal scores Carpenter created for his films Halloween, The Fog, and Assault on Precinct 13, but this is a much heavier, riff-driven enterprise. Carpenter is a firm believer that music plays a major role in what really makes something scary. That’s first and foremost,” the director says. “It’s all about making the music work.” “This is somewhat different sounding stuff that we’ve done, but it’s done with the same desire in mind,” he adds. “In other words, put this thing on and imagine you’re watching a movie. That’s what we want you to do.”

Daniel Davies’ soaring, snaky guitars take center stage on opener “Primeval,” “Elevator,” and the metal masterpiece “Lord of the Underground” while John Carpenter and Cody Carpenter’s synths take the lead on the ominous “Desolation in the Underworld,” the plaintive “Death of the Mapmaker,” and even converge with strings on “Abandoned Cathedral.”

Whereas the Lost Themes albums were written as scores to movies of the mind, Cathedral scores the first original graphic novel written by Carpenter, his wife and long-time creative partner, producer and editor Sandy King, and writer Sean Sobczak, published by Storm King Comics."

items.body:
Following the tradition of Derek Bailey, Henry Kraiser and Sonny Sharrock albums on Celluloid Records, the label is releasing this abstract and mysterious instrumental album, made under a cryptic name: AA in Reverse, by nqthqn.

"Recorded shortly after last year’s Ghostbox Cowboy, released on Tailnia Records out of China, this new effort digs deeper into what critics describe as buzzards circling the half-dead body of Harry Dean Stanton in Paris, Texas. The project curiously explores what it might be like to create no-wave abstract guitar music by a campfire, as inaugurated by Arto Lindsay, Loren Connors or John Fahey.

AA in Reverse was recorded and engineered by David Akerman (Robin Hitchcock, Dead Farmers) at Golden Retriever Studios (Parcels, Cate Le Bon, Courtney Barnett) in Marrickville."

items.body:
Roy Montgomery and Martha Skye Murphy extend their thing on 'Nebular', penning a suite of widescreen dreampop epics that harness all their separate strengths into a fizzing artmelt -  tipped FFO Cocteau Twins & Harold Budd, Flying Saucer Attack, Jessamine and lovesliescrushing.

It didn't take much for Montgomery and Murphy to connect. All Murphy did was include one of Mongomery's songs on a mixtape and the conversations that followed led them to spot harmonies in their approaches to music: they both recorded to a Tascam multitrack recorder, for one. And if you've been following either artist, you'll have noticed their collaborations bubbling up through the cracks in the last few years. Murphy appeared on Montgomery's lush 'At Dawn' lathe cut 7" in 2023 and on his 2024 Roy Montgomery and Friends album 'Broken Heart Surgery (An Agony In Six Fits)', while Montgomery lent his distinct tone to Murphy's 2024 debut album 'Um', playing on the excellent 'Need'. It was all leading up to 'Nebular'; the two artists might be based on opposite sides of the globe, with Montgomery in New Zealand and Murphy in the UK, but they sound fully converged on this perfectly-pruned five tracker, developing a sound that's both related to their respective solo signatures and presents something new, too.

Montgomery's well-worn tone is present, forming a pillowy bed of post-Florian Fricke ambiance, yet it doesn't sound like any of his recent releases. And although Murphy's powerful, operatic tones were just as crucial to the success of 'Um', they're used differently here, reshaped into elongated, wordless traces and textures. Somehow, as weighty as it is, it works like a lengthy introduction before 'Nebular' asserts itself in earnest on 'Cloudburst'. Singing more confidently, Murphy augments her breathy vocals with stacked, dreamy textures that wisp and wind around Montgomery's strums. Maybe we can link it to Grouper or possibly even Julia Holter, but the way the duo treat the mixing and recording makes it sound older and grungier, like some lost 4AD release that never made it to the pressing plant.

The record hinges around the 17-minute 'The Play of Light and Dark', a side of rhythmic, chiming ambience from Montgomery that Murphy helps sculpt into a muggy mantra, vocalising unrestrainedly and shaping a sound that's refreshingly human. It doesn't shift so much as it melts, changing only slightly to draw you into its aura. When Mary Lattimore shows up on the finale 'At Dusk', it's a gorgeous, necessary palate cleanser.
items._cn_summary: Roy Montgomery与Martha Skye Murphy合作专辑《Nebular》共五首曲目，以widescreen dream pop为骨架，融合ambient质感与吉他氛围。两位艺术家相隔千里，通过Tascam多轨录音设备找到共鸣点。Murphy的人声被重塑为延长的无词纹理，而非传统演绎；Montgomery则提供了熟悉的post-Florian Fricke式氛围铺垫。17分钟的核心曲目《The Play of Light and Dark》以节奏性的钟鸣氛围为基础，Murphy放开声线塑形为潮湿的咒语式人声。终曲《At Dusk》邀请Mary Lattimore以竖琴出现，提供清新的色彩过渡。整体录音质感刻意保留粗粝与年代感，模仿4AD厂牌未发行的遗失作品。

items.body:
First re-pressing in years of Mark Ernestus & Moritz Von Oswald’s divine, final Rhythm & Sound release, heeling to tradition with a one-riddim album focussed on its carousel of roots reggae legends; Sugar Minott, Paul St. Hilaire, Willi Williams, Jah Cotton, Bobbo Shanti, and more

In 2005 Rhythm & Sound capped their holy mountain catalogue with ‘See Mi Yah’, a 7 x 7” set and LP which completed a 10 year run of inspired dub productions with their purest offering to the form. At the time, younger ears to their music would be left perplexed by the lack of instrumental variation - but any others with a little knowledge of one-riddim set traditions knew it was their ultimate ode to roots reggae fundamentals, after respectfully messing with the style & pattern across the Burial Mix 10”s (as collected in ‘w/ The Artists’), and the more radical 12” mutations of the Rhythm & Sound series, proper, since 1996 (not to mention birthing dub house-techno before that).     

Seeing off the project in fine style, Ernestus & Von Oswald gave studio time to their favourite vocalists, generating a slew of original performances displaying the range and depth of roots reggae’s elders and contemporary torch carriers on their signature backdrop of air-trodding bass and powdered dub chords. We were blessed to distribute it in the UK at the time, so many of these cuts are hard etched to the memory, from the ghostly croon of Willi Williams’ title piece thru the gruff gravitas of Bobbo Shanti, the duet between Ras Donovan & Ras Perez, and of course Sugar Minott’s mellifluous reggae soul.

In the year following ‘See Mi Yah’, Rhythm & Sound were naturally elected to edit and master a re-up of The Congos & Friends’ one-riddim album ’Fisherman Style’ for our then warehouse neighbours Blood & Fire Records, sealing their era of roots reflection by appropriately saluting the originators, in parallel to their Wackies reissue scheme, and before Ernestus (and Mark Ainley) would go on to found the more digi-devoted reissue label, Dug Out. Some 20 years of satisfaction later, time has proven this album holds its meditative weight.
items._genre: dub / roots reggae / minimal electronic / dub techno
items._cn_summary: 这是Rhythm & Sound（Mark Ernestus与Moritz Von Oswald）的最终专辑《See Mi Yah》首次多年后再版发行。两人以dub techno先驱闻名，此作回归根源雷鬼传统，采用单一riddim结构，邀请Sugar Minott、Paul St. Hilaire、Willi Williams等多位牙买加歌手在标志性的低频贝斯与粉末感dub和弦上进行演绎。专辑剥离器乐变化，以冥想式的极简手法致敬根源雷鬼基本范式，是此前Burial Mix系列与12寸激进变奏探索之后的纯粹化回归。评论指出，发行二十年后的今天，这张作品依然保持着沉稳的重量感，展现了电子制作人对根源传统的尊重与深度理解。

items.tags: 書籍 ジャズ intoxicate 2026 June 書籍 書籍 小室敬幸 MILES DAVIS
items.excerpt: 今年、生誕100周年をむかえたマイルス・デイヴィス。マイルスについて書かれた本が数多く世に出たけれど、これほどまでに彼の音楽の中身にフォーカスされたものは他にない。アルバムごとの演奏を事細かに分析し、マイルスの即興演奏への向き合い方の変容を捉えることで、ジャズミュージシャンとしてどのように新しいものを生み出そうとしていたのかが浮き彫りになる。また、ライヴの映像での仕草やアルバムとのセットリストの違いなど音の外側にも目を向け、彼の思考に迫ろうとしているのが面白い。やや音楽に精通した人向けの内容ではあるものの、マイルスの音源を聴きながら楽しんでほしい一冊である。

items._cn_summary: 这是一本关于爵士巨匠小室敬幸所著《迈尔斯·戴维斯研究入门》的书评。迈尔斯·戴维斯诞生100周年之际，相关书籍纷纷出版，而本书的独特之处在于聚焦其音乐本身的内容。该书对戴维斯每张专辑的演奏进行了细致分析，追踪了他即兴演奏方法的演变历程，揭示了他作为爵士音乐家如何持续追求创新的过程。此外，作者还将视线扩展到声音之外，考察现场影像中的演奏姿态以及现场与录音室曲目编排的差异，以此深入探究戴维斯的音乐思维。书评指出该书偏向有一定音乐知识的读者，建议在聆听戴维斯录音的同时阅读此书。
