items.body: Review by OlyaBeginner — Listening to 'Never for Ever' felt like entering a strange emotional and almost theatrical world. I am not an expert in Kate Bush's music, so I approached the album mostly through my own feelings, images, and associations. What impressed me most is how freely she plays with her voice which becomes almost another instrument.1. BabooshkaA very playful and energetic song with a bright sound that immediately sparks emotions. There is something almost mischievous about it. At first, the music feels light and catchy, but underneath it there is a rather bitter and complicated story about love, jealousy, and mistrust. I really like this contrast between the almost cheerful sound and the darker emotions behind it.2. DeliusThis song is very strange and mysterious, but in a beautiful way. It creates an almost magical atmosphere, as if the listener is entering another world. The sound feels peaceful but also slightly unreal. It elevates the soul to another level and leaves me with the feeling of being somewhere far away from ordinary life.3. Blow AwayMy favourite song on the album. There is such an interesting play with Kate Bush's voice here. She seems to move between different emotional states, and the song feels almost theatrical. It charges me with energy while making me feel something tragic and elevated at the same time. There is a strange combination of excitement and sadness that I find incredibly beautiful.4. All We Ever Look ForA very strong song with a lot of emotional power. It feels as if it can touch something deep inside the listener. To be honest, I did not understand the meaning of it at first. After thinking about it more, I see it as a song about family, inheritance, and the things people spend their lives searching for. We inherit things from our parents, leave the family home, and then continue searching for love, security, meaning, or something that will finally make us feel complete.I especially like the musical instruments and the sound design. The song feels almost restless, as if the music itself is constantly searching for something that it cannot quite find.5. EgyptThis one feels mysterious and theatrical. It has a strong progressive-rock feeling to me, although it also sounds experimental and almost cinematic. The music creates the impression of travelling through a strange landscape. I like how different this song feels from the more intimate pieces on the album.6. The Wedding ListSuch a great song. I love the dramatic progression and the way the story unfolds. Kate Bush almost seems to be telling a fairy tale before sleep, but it is a very dark fairy tale. The music gradually becomes more intense, and the story feels increasingly dramatic. I really enjoy how she combines storytelling, theatrical performance, and music.7. ViolinSuper rock'n'roll and incredibly energetic. This song feels wild and almost uncontrollable. It has a completely different energy from the quieter and more mysterious songs on the album. I especially like the feeling of movement and excitement it creates.8. The Infant KissSuper creepy.The song is deeply unsettling. What makes it even more disturbing is the contrast between the beautiful, almost delicate sound and the uncomfortable subject matter. It creates a feeling that something is not quite right, even when the music itself sounds beautiful.9. Night Scented StockExtremely beautiful. This song creates such a delicate and almost dreamlike atmosphere. It feels as if the music is floating rather than moving forward. Once again, Kate Bush's voice contributes enormously to this feeling. It elevates my soul and creates a sense of peace and mystery.10. Army DreamersI love this song. It is heartbreaking and sad, but there is also something very beautiful and restrained about it. The sound feels almost permeated by sadness.The song is about a mother grieving for her son who has died as a soldier. But listening to it today, I could not help thinking about my own generation. Many young people were raised with the idea that the world was moving toward peace, cooperation, and friendship between countries. Hearing a song about a young life being destroyed by war therefore feels painfully relevant today.What makes the song especially powerful is that it does not sound aggressive. It sounds almost gentle, which makes the tragedy even stronger.11. BreathingThis is probably the song that shocked me the most.The song is written from the perspective of a fetus that is still inside the womb but is already aware of the terrifying world outside. The fetus is frightened by nuclear destruction and wonders what kind of world it is going to be born into.The line about dying "without" breathing is especially powerful because the word remains incomplete until the very end. Only then do we understand what is missing: breathing itself. The song connects the most basic condition of life with the possibility of nuclear destruction.And this is what makes the song so frighteningly relevant. It was written decades ago, but the fear behind it has not disappeared. It is deeply disturbing that humanity is still capable of threatening itself with weapons that could destroy the world. The song makes me think about how reckless it is to treat such a possibility as a political instrument.So, Never for Ever feels to me like an album about things that are difficult to explain directly: love, fear, family, death, war, desire, memory, and the strange feeling of being alive. What I admire most is her ability to transform emotions into characters, voices, and almost theatrical scenes, so the listener can experience the world she is creating.

items._cn_summary: 凯特·布什这张1980年的专辑展现了极强的艺术个性与人声实验性，将声音本身当作独立乐器进行自由运用。乐评特别强调了这种跨越传统流行结构的创作方式：明快旋律表面下暗藏嫉妒与不信任的苦涩叙事，平静音色营造出超现实氛围，戏剧化的能量与悲剧感交织。专辑呈现出近乎戏剧化的叙事结构，从暗黑童话到狂野摇滚能量，从家庭传承的深刻冥想到神秘东方意象的探索。整体评价认为这是一张兼具情感深度与声音设计巧思的作品，凯特·布什在流行框架内注入了前卫艺术的灵魂，人声作为核心乐器的处理方式以及戏剧化的叙事手法是这张专辑的核心特色。

items.body: Jabulile Majola sings “Baba Wethu” as a dove worn down by its journey, “Ngijuba elifuna indawo yokuphumula“, crossing hills and gullies through steady rain in search of somewhere to rest. When the bird’s strength gives out it calls up to heaven, the same cry each time over a marching chant, “Ulaphi sekonakala“, “where are you when things fall apart”, to the Father the isiZulu title names. The bird calling out for a Father is a boy who was left. The lyric opens on “Uthando lwangishiya ngisase mncane”, love left him while he was still a child, and he sings it from his own life: his mother vanished when he was days old, and by the age of two a pastor’s family was raising him among 26 children in rural Greytown, KwaZulu-Natal. He took the name she left him. It is all he has of her. The prayer turns before it ends. Majola reaches for a hand, “esangithunga ndawonye”, the hand that stitched him together, and asks it to lead him through the mist and across to the far side, “Ithemba eliyongiwelisa ngaphesheya”, the hope that will carry him over. He opened the song too worn to go on and ends it asking to be carried the rest of the way. He wrote “Baba Wethu” with his oldest brother, Levit Phungula. The song opens IPASI, his coming debut album, and follows his 2025 EP Isitifiketi. The live take comes from the Baxter Theatre in Rondebosch, Cape Town, where Ross Dorkin of Cape Town afropop trio Beatenberg joins Majola on bass. Stream and listen to “Baba Wethu” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Jabulile Majola – Baba Wethu (Live at The Baxter Theatre) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评围绕南非歌手Jabulile Majola的现场录音作品展开，歌曲以"Baba Wethu"（我们的父亲）为题，用祖鲁语写成，风格定位于非洲流行与灵性灵魂乐的交汇处。乐评用诗意的笔触描绘了歌曲的叙事结构：一只疲惫的鸽子穿越风雨寻找栖息之地，象征着创作者自幼被母亲遗弃、由牧师家庭抚养的个人经历。歌词从倾诉转向祈祷，结尾处请求被引领跨越迷雾。整首作品以行进式的吟唱为基底，bass伴奏来自开普敦afropop三重奏Beatenberg成员Ross Dorkin。该曲将收录于Majola即将发行的首张专辑IPASI，展现了南非原住民语言书写与个人生命叙事相结合的音乐路径。

items.body: 6YPAH is a Slovenian/Italian duo releasing their debut album here. It appears to be a conceptual work inspired by the early years of the Soviet space program and the space race with the USA. The duo crafted this six-track album primarily using analog equipment. The opening track immediately transports us to a bygone musical era, perfectly matching the album’s concept. Clear Krautrock influences are evident, with the psychedelic guitar taking center stage. Gradually, a balance develops between guitar and electronics, with the warm analog textures adding further depth. The music consistently evokes a sense of nostalgia, at times leaning toward an ’80s aesthetic and even incorporating touches of Wave-Pop. Vocals are present throughout, although they serve more as an additional layer than as the main focus of the compositions. This strikes me as the kind of album that truly benefits from a visual component, allowing its concept to unfold to its fullest. It is a highly commendable debut that will especially appeal to a discerning audience. (Rating:6½). Listen to “Vedno S Tabo”: Vedno S Tabo by 6YPAH About 6YPAH 6YPAH is a Slovenian duo formed in Nova Gorica in 2009 by singer and keyboardist Jani Toplak and guitarist and bassist Giorgio Multineddu. The project calls itself “transboundary,” pairing Slovenian songwriting with a base that stretches across the nearby Italian border into Gorizia. 6YPAH mixes synthwave with krautrock and 1970s and 1980s German electronic influences, and sings in Slovene. The duo self-released its first recording, “Electronic Visions Across The Border” (CDr, catalog RSSCD02), in 2023. 6YPAH then signed to Final Muzik for “Prozorno Mesto,” a concept album inspired by the Soviet Buran space program and the space race with the United States. Bandcamp lists the release date as 7 April 2026, while Discogs dates the release to 2025. The album was recorded and mixed at Resounding Sounds Studio in Gorizia, Italy, and mastered by Gregor Zemljic in Ljubljana, Slovenia. Guitarist Matteo Birsa performs a guest solo on “Vedno S Tabo.” The album’s limited CD edition is capped at 200 copies, tying this release to the duo’s ongoing work built around analog synthesizers and Cold War-era imagery.
items._cn_summary: 斯洛文尼亚/意大利跨界二人组6YPAH的首张专辑以苏联太空计划为概念框架，全专辑通过模拟设备录制，共六首曲目。音乐风格扎根于七十年代德国Krautrock传统，迷幻吉他占据主导地位，随后逐渐让位于温暖的模拟合成器质感，形成吉他与电子之间的平衡。人声贯穿始终但退居为音色层之一，整体弥漫着浓重的怀旧情绪，间或融入八十年代新浪潮流行质感。专辑以斯洛文尼亚语演唱，概念与冷战时期苏联航天形象紧密关联。评论指出该作需要一个视觉载体来完整呈现其概念，适合口味精细的听众。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: Analog Africa厂牌推出的第44号合辑，收录贝宁歌手Antoine Dougb与Orchestre Poly-Rythmo于1977至1982年间合作的作品。Dougbe以双手拍击大腿演绎Cavacha节奏著称，其风格根植于伏都教传统，鼓手Belobi Meridjo创造的火车节拍模式曾蔓延至整个刚果流行乐坛。音乐在根源与时代之间游走：吉他带着塑料质感的光泽，合成器铺底，清晰呈现古巴颂乐与刚果伦巴的双重影响。专辑以合成器音床开场，闪亮吉他与镲片主导的律动交织，中段吉他分裂出多向线条，合成器再次铺底形成张力。多首曲目以牛铃持续敲击、鼻音人声呼应与紧凑循环段为核心结构，整体录音生涯虽短暂却密度极高，展现西非都市流行乐在七十年代末的复杂面貌。

items.album: Event Review: WOMAD 2026 @ Neston Park (Corsham, Wiltshire; Thursday 23rd to Sunday 26th July 2026)

items.body: There is a certain tenor a WOMAD stalwart comes to expect: a practiced routine, a beaten track past well-known landmarks, a familiarity akin to coming home. Sometimes it’s good to mix it up a bit. This July marked the festival’s first edition in a new location just up the road from Charlton Park, its much-loved site for 17 happy years before taking a break in 2025. Organisers have been quick to reassure returnees that they’ll find the new spot welcoming and Neston Park, just half an hour away in Corsham, does indeed have a home-from-home feel, the flutter of those familiar flags helping crowds settle quickly into the weekend. Some old favourites are missing: the d&b Soundscape stage with its state-of-the-art surround-sound experience; late night party venue Molly’s Bar; the Ecotricity stage, a cosy woodland spot for daytime respite or atmospheric after-dark shows; the magical Hidden Forest lit up by Luke Jerram’s Moon; the World of Science (a niche interest perhaps but a favourite, inevitably, of some). WOMAD kicks off at its brand new site at Neston Park, marking a new chapter for the independent World of Music and Dance Festival – Photo © garryjonesphotography So it is left to the music to carry the show and here the new compactness comes into its own, the smaller tents packed with hidden gems and standout performances of the festival which has not skimped on its musical programme at least. The main stages offer up a mixed bag of hits and misses, occasionally mired by murky sound and drab set design. On the World Stage the effervescent Derya Yıldırım, her voice in turns aching, wistful and full of soul, is supported by the psychedelic squelchy synth and phenomenally groovy rhythm section of her Grup Şimşek. It is sun-drenched and beautiful, augmented by her call for freedom, cultural strength and acceptance for those dwelling in the diaspora. Bristol’s Ishmael Ensemble seem warm in their black outfits, camouflaged against a black stage and backdrop and playing directly into the sun’s heat. Perhaps this explains the low energy feel of both band and scattered crowd. Their jazz-inspired saxophone-and-synth jams with Rituals ‘Orchestra’ (comprising two violins, a harp and a cello) is lacking oomph. A smaller stage may well have inspired bigger vibes. Reggae legend Barrington Levy takes to the World Stage at WOMAD festival – Friday – Photo © garryjonesphotography Reggae icon Barrington Levy is welcomed by a vast, multi-generational crowd and while there are a few unconvincing moments from a seemingly under-rehearsed band (as well as a smattering of problematic lyrical content sometimes associated with reggae that predates the 80s), his voice is as smooth and powerful as ever, his scatting as wild and his strut as convincing, especially on 2025’s ‘A Fi Yuh’. Eventually, the crowd is galvanised into repeatedly requesting “run the track” while Levy teases ‘Black Roses’ and ‘Here I Come’ until well beyond his stage time, berating the MC for clock-watching and singing on until his mic is turned off. The night’s headliner Greentea Peng calls “I love you Barry” and apes his vocal riffing throughout her glorious 90-minute show. An all-round class act, her band provide tasteful support for her elegant, honey-smothered r’n’b, with a high calibre all-female brass section ramping up the energy and spectacle. Greentea Peng headlining WOMAD Festival – Friday – Photo © garryjonesphotography On Saturday, Mixanteña de Santa Cecilia from Mexico City treat a packed Big Top to a classic slice of WOMAD with a high energy fusion of costumed dancers, ritualistic set pieces, eight-piece brass section and percussion. Their mix of cumbia, bossa nova and boleros is full of life, while joyful dancers in long-haired ram-horned headdress and twirling petticoats cause a stir when their bull puppet is sent in to dance with the crowd. It is experiences like these that keep people returning year on year. Similarly, Bénin International Musical provide the perfect sunny soundtrack to a hot afternoon, the disco pop harmonies of Say She She floating across the field give the sense that all is right with this world of music and dance, and Nakibembe Xylophone Troupe are hotly tipped as this year’s mustn’t-miss sensation. Ugandan Nakimbembe Xylophone Troupe bring their 3 metres long embaire to WOMAD, the largest instrument to grace the festivals stages, played by 6 members – Photo © garryjonesphotography But it is the Sunflower stage, a stretch tent conveniently located to break up the just-too-arduous walk between the two main stages, that provides the weekend’s first nugget of pure gold. Tamer Nafar, one third of Palestinian hip hop trio DAM, is flanked for this solo appearance by a beat maker and exquisite Arabic-influenced electric violinist. Nafar is a warm presence with powerful words, throwing out politically charged statements and personal anecdotes with equal emotive power. His latest record, In the Name of the Father, the Imam and John Lennon, references the two CDs his dad would play when driving him to underground rap clubs: the Beatles and the Quran. “But we don’t have to imagine there’s no country”, a defiant teenage Nafar said back then, but he’s retained his love of the seminal Liverpudlians. LYR (Land Yacht Regatta, inexplicably) draw big numbers to that same tent, primarily to catch celebrity poet Simon Armitage in his new musical guise, his downbeat musings backed by pulsing bass and suitably moody, introspective soundscapes. His dry Yorkshire humour goes down well between songs and the crowd responds enthusiastically to the band’s paean to libraries, ‘The Enlightenment’, in particular. Tamer Nafar, a vanguard of Arabic Hip-Hop, the Palestinian rapper living in Israel performs a selection of tracks discussing Middle East politics & life at WOMAD – Friday – Photo © garryjonesphotography The even smaller Village Stage, tucked away in a corner next to second mainstage the Big Top, boasts some of the best acts of the weekend. For only their second live show, Romanian seven-piece Lăutăresele Șaraimanic pull out all the stops with high glamour and captivating dancing drawing on the Turkish and Roma heritage of their homeland. Accordionist Mituș Răducanu, the oldest group member, steals the show with his delighted toothy grins. Later in the day, Belarusian Yegor Zabelov keeps the audience riveted with his expansive world-building, pushing the accordion to new creative limits with drones, sound walls and percussion sounds. And sparky Portuguese solo artist Ana Lua Caiano grabs attention with her melodramatic delivery, then holds it with impressive looping of synth, percussion and voice into multilayered epics of fiery emotion. A stunned audience of all ages watch each song construction with awe, then explode in applause as Caiano expresses her deep delight and gratitude. Lautaresele Saraimanic at Village Stage performing at WOMAD Festival – Friday – Photo © garryjonesphotography The sentiment was one that emanated across the site as another WOMAD was put to bed. Dynamic, welcoming, vibrating with fighting spirit and above all full of joy and connection, the 2026 edition served as a reminder of the role the festival plays in building community and educating through creativity. Pre-sale tickets for 2027 have already sold out. Perhaps this year’s success will instil organisers with the confidence to bring back some of the site’s sorely missed old favourites; or, more in keeping with the culture of the event, to surprise us with something wholly new and unexpected.   Pre-sale tickets for 2027 have already sold out, but you can keep in the loop for the next batch over at womad.co.uk     Photos © garryjonesphotography The post Event Review: WOMAD 2026 @ Neston Park (Corsham, Wiltshire; Thursday 23rd to Sunday 26th July 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Swiss avant-garde project KiKu will release its new album Suzhou / It’s All The Rage on Everest Records on September 25, 2026, on LP and CD. The album features Blixa Bargeld, founder and vocalist of Einstürzende Neubauten, and Berlin-based rapper and vocalist Black Cracker. “Suzhou / It’s All The Rage” is built as a diptych: two distinct halves held together by a shared musical architecture of trumpet, drums, sampler and electronics. The digital release and CD present the work as a continuous eight-track album. On vinyl, the dual structure becomes physical, with Side A carrying “Suzhou” featuring Bargeld and Side B carrying “It’s All The Rage” featuring Black Cracker. On “Suzhou”, Bargeld’s vocals move between speech, song, whisper and abstract vocal gesture across four tracks shaped by space, tension and control. On “It’s All The Rage”, Black Cracker’s vocals take a more percussive, volatile and immediate approach across the remaining four tracks. The tracklist runs: Suzhou – KiKu feat. Blixa Bargeld – Orlando’s Victory – 4:06 – The Number of the Millibeast – 4:48 – Suzhou (XX XY YX YY) – 4:16 – Nonsense Rock’n’Roll – 4:58 It’s All The Rage – KiKu feat. Black Cracker – Bull Whip – 3:36 – Leaping Bull (Chicago) – 5:05 – The Running of the Bulls – 3:50 – Sleeping Bull (Woke) – 4:32 Vocals and lyrics on tracks 1-4 are by Blixa Bargeld. Vocals and lyrics on tracks 5-8 are by Black Cracker. David Doyon plays guitar on tracks 2-4, and Cyril Regamey plays drums and sampler throughout. Bargeld’s vocals were recorded by Boris Wilsdorf at andereBaustelle Tonstudio, Berlin. Black Cracker recorded his own vocals, which were edited and mixed by Jane Arnison in Berlin. Drums were recorded by Antoine Estoppey at Blend Studio, Lutry, and trumpet and computer parts by Yannick Barman at Printemps Digital Studio, Monthey. The album was mixed by Barman and mastered by Estoppey at Blend Studio. Artwork and graphic design are by Cédric Raccio at La Fabrik, Monthey, and the photo of Bargeld is by Thomas Rabsch. About KiKu KiKu was founded in 2003 in Sion, Switzerland, by trumpeter and composer Yannick Barman and drummer and percussionist Cyril Regamey. The pair started as an acoustic improvisation duo, and their sound turned toward electronic music during a run of concerts at the Théâtre de l’Oriental in Vevey in February 2003. Since then, KiKu has operated as an open, modular formation that changes line-up and musical language with each project, working across contemporary jazz, electronic music, rock, improvised music and experimental sound art. The group has toured internationally, performing at jazz clubs and festivals across Europe and Asia as well as in Australia, and has previously collaborated with Blixa Bargeld and Black Cracker on the albums “Marcher sur la tête” (2015) and “Eng, Düster und Bang” (2017), both on Everest Records. Bargeld founded Einstürzende Neubauten in Berlin in 1980 and was also a member of Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds from 1983 to 2003. Black Cracker, born Ellison Glenn in Anniston, Alabama, is a rapper, producer and vocalist based in Berlin who also performs with the Swiss jazz trio Grand Pianoramax. “Suzhou / It’s All The Rage” extends KiKu’s collaboration with both vocalists into a new full-length release on Everest Records.
items._cn_summary: 瑞士实验组合KiKu将于2026年9月通过Everest Records发行新专辑，专辑以双联画结构呈现：上半部"苏州"邀请Einstürzende Neubauten主脑Blixa Bargeld参与，其人声在言语、吟唱、低语与抽象发声之间游走；下半部"全凭这股劲"则与柏林说唱歌手Black Cracker合作，以打击感强烈、即兴而直接的方式展开。两部分共享小号、鼓、采样器与电子设备构成的音乐骨架。KiKu由小号手Yannick Barman与鼓手Cyril Regamey于2003年创立，以开放式模块编制在不同项目中变换阵容与语言，跨越当代爵士、电子、摇滚、即兴与实验声音艺术等领域。专辑在瑞士蒙泰与洛特里等多地录音，由Barman混音、Estoppey母带处理。文章为新闻稿性质，缺乏主观评论深度，但所描述的跨界合作架构与实验气质值得关注。

The 13-track digital and CD release ships on Compact Disc in a jewel box with an 8-page booklet of photography and in a limited deluxe CD box with bonus postcards and stickers; the vinyl LP, pressed on solid pink, carries an 11-track cut, “11 Stitches,” made to fit the format, with the full 13-track album included
items.body: Ayria, the Toronto electro-pop, EBM and futurepop project of Jennifer Parkin, will release the album “13 Stitches” on October 2, 2026 through Artoffact Records. The 13-track digital and CD release ships on Compact Disc in a jewel box with an 8-page booklet of photography and in a limited deluxe CD box with bonus postcards and stickers; the vinyl LP, pressed on solid pink, carries an 11-track cut, “11 Stitches,” made to fit the format, with the full 13-track album included as a digital download. Ayria bring an EBM and futurepop sound that mixes stomping electronic rhythms with pop hooks and personal, confrontational lyrics, and Parkin describes “13 Stitches” as a record of personal rebirth. The album was produced and mastered by Sebastian R. Komor at Xenomorph Production Studio, with additional contributions from Komor and Joe Byer of v01d. Its tracklist runs “Feeding Your Monsters,” “Turn of the Tide,” “Not My First Time,” “Long Gone,” “Vicious World,” “Manic,” “Antihero,” “Trickle Truth,” “Don’t Ever Touch Me Again,” “Overturn,” “We’re Not Relevant,” “Mr. Morals” and “Turn Into Gold.” The vinyl edition omits “We’re Not Relevant” and “Turn Into Gold” to fit the format. 13 Stitches by Ayria Ayria’s ‘Vicious World’ single ahead of ’13 Stitches’ Ayria shared “Vicious World” as the lead single from “13 Stitches,” with an official video pairing the track’s EBM stomp and repetition with dark, visceral visuals. About Ayria Ayria is the project of Toronto musician Jennifer Parkin, formed in 2003. Her debut album, “Debris,” followed later that year, with “My Revenge on the World” and “Flicker” in 2005, “Hearts for Bullets” on Alfa Matrix in 2008, “Plastic Makes Perfect” in 2013 and “Paper Dolls” in 2016, the last of which Side-Line covered as it was announced on CD, 2CD and fuchsia vinyl after the single “Feed Her to the Wolves.” Parkin discussed her approach to songwriting and production in a 2016 interview with Side-Line, and toured North America and the UK alongside Inertia that same year. Ayria signed to Artoffact Records in 2020 and most recently released the “Vicious World” EP, which Side-Line reviewed, ahead of “13 Stitches,” due October 2, 2026.
items._cn_summary: 本文为专辑发行公告而非乐评。Ayria（Jennifer Parkin）将推出新专辑《13 Stitches》，由Artoffact Records于2026年10月发行。作品延续EBM与futurepop路线，以强劲电子节奏搭配流行旋律，歌词带有个人化且对抗性色彩，Parkin将专辑定位为个人重生的记录。制作由Sebastian R. Komor在Xenomorph Production Studio完成，Joe Byer（v01d）亦有参与。发行版本包含数字、CD及粉色乙烯基，CD附带摄影册页，限量版含明信片与贴纸；黑胶版因时长限制精简为11首。先行单曲《Vicious World》以EBM节奏与重复结构搭配暗黑视觉影像。作为来自多伦多的电子音乐人，Parkin自2003年起持续创作，此前已在Alfa Matrix等厂牌发行多张作品。文章内容偏向资讯性质，缺乏对音乐本身的深入分析与聆听评价。

items.body: Schrödinger, the post-punk duo from Mexico City, released their second studio album, “International Decay,” digitally on July 26, 2026 through Swiss Dark Nights. The label follows with physical editions on September 4, 2026: a regular black vinyl LP, a limited white vinyl LP with red splatters capped at 250 copies, and a CD in digipak with a booklet containing lyrics and additional artwork. Schrödinger is the project of brothers Carlos and Ernesto Carapia, who mix post-punk, gothic rock and darkwave with delayed and reverberated guitars and synthesizers over cold, chaotic vocals. “International Decay” runs eight tracks: “Broken Cities,” “The Void,” “Ghost Nation,” “Eclipse of Faith,” “Metal Rain,” “Eleventh Hour,” “Caotica Penumbra” (featuring the Argentine gothic rock band Euroshima) and “Black Room.” International Decay by Schrödinger Schrödinger describe ‘International Decay’ as a more forceful record Schrödinger stated: “There’s a very noticeable change compared to the previous album. On the first album, we opted for a more minimalist sound, where space and atmosphere played a fundamental role, without losing that nocturnal identity that characterises the band. On this new album, there’s a clear evolution towards a more mature, solid and forceful sound. The compositions, arrangements and production were developed with a more precise approach, seeking greater depth, power and cohesion in each track. We believe it retains the essence of Schrödinger, but presents it with a more defined identity and a much more consolidated sound.” “Caotica Penumbra” features Euroshima, the Argentine gothic rock and darkwave band formed in Buenos Aires in 1986 by Fabián Iribarne, José Wyszogrod, Ricardo Parrabere and vocalist Wanda, whose album “Gala” was reissued on vinyl by Dark Entries Records in 2022. About Schrödinger Schrödinger formed in Mexico City around brothers Carlos Carapia (guitars, programming, synthesizers) and Ernesto Carapia (vocals, bass, electronics, synthesizers). After close to a decade of live activity, the duo issued their debut full-length, “Last Days on Earth,” in October 2020 through Swiss Dark Nights, an album built on the chaos of the human mind with reverbed, delay-heavy guitars over a dense, melancholic atmosphere. “International Decay,” released digitally on July 26, 2026 and following on vinyl and CD on September 4, 2026, is Schrödinger’s second studio album and continues the band’s work with Swiss Dark Nights.
items._cn_summary: Schrödinger 是来自墨西哥城的二人后朋克项目，由兄弟 Carlos 和 Ernesto Carapia 组成。他们的第二张专辑《International Decay》延续了延迟与混响吉他、冷峻失序人声结合合成器的暗潮美学。乐队将这张唱片描述为从极简氛围向更成熟、强劲声音的进化，编曲与制作更趋精密，寻求更深的层次与凝聚力。专辑收录八首曲目，包括与阿根廷哥特摇滚乐队 Euroshima 合作的《Caotica Penumbra》。实体发行由瑞士独立厂牌 Swiss Dark Nights 推出，包括黑胶与限量彩色版本。该作品作为暗潮类型内的常规延续，融合了墨西哥与阿根廷的拉美地下场景视角，但在声音创新与跨界融合层面缺乏明显的实验性突破。

items.body: French solo project Morphoex released the album “Méta Langages” on January 6, 2026, a 12-track record built around voices, field recordings and synthesizers, recorded on magnetic tape at a farm studio in Normandy. Méta Langages by MORPHOEX Morphoex’s ‘Méta Langages’ album “Méta Langages” is the seventh full-length released under the Morphoex name and the first to be almost entirely sung. The album is a concept record centered on voice, transmission and language, running as a continuous, uninterrupted listen. It includes twelve tracks: “Vagues sidérales,” “Schizodrome,” “Méta langages,” “Listen to the New Noise,” “Reality Is False,” “Tnemetohcuhc,” “Confuse Science Illustration,” “Black and White Lines,” “Vengeance Is Silence,” “Kinshasa,” “Toniki” and “Après un cataclysme.” Music and words are by Isthmaël Baudry throughout, except for “Schizodrome,” composed by Zaäk Årandi. Urban and nature sounds were captured through field recording, and the vocal and synthesizer parts were recorded onto magnetic tape at a studio set up on a farm in Normandy’s Eure department. Cédric Moglia recorded and mastered the album. About Morphoex Morphoex is the solo project of French artist Isthmaël Baudry, based in Rouen. Baudry also sings in the post-punk band Spleen XXX and in the project Love in Cage, whose track appeared in a Side-Line compilation. “Méta Langages” is Morphoex’s seventh album under the project name and its first mostly-sung release, following earlier releases including “An Imaginary Being.”

items._cn_summary: 法国单人项目Morphoex于2026年1月发布第七张全长专辑《Méta Langages》，这是该项目中首次几乎完全以人声为核心的作品。整张专辑围绕声音、传递与语言的概念展开，包含十二首曲目，建议作为一段连续不间断的聆听体验。制作上以田野录音捕捉城市与自然声响，人声与合成器部分在诺曼底一家农场工作室以磁带录制完成。Cédric Moglia负责录音与母带处理。词曲均由Isthmaël Baudry独立完成，仅《Schizodrome》一曲由Zaäk Årandi作曲。Baudry同时在法国后朋克乐队Spleen XXX与Love in Cage项目中参与演唱。专辑概念聚焦于人声作为媒介与语言的反思，磁带录音与田野采样的结合赋予作品手工质感与空间感。

items.body:
Death Is Not The End return to the soul-stir sound of deep south Sacred Harp Singers in 1993 - although it could feasibly be any time since the advent of portable tape recording - in the blessed company of the Union Grove Baptist Church, Ozark, Alabama. Feels just right in this humidity…

The Wiregrass Singers' Dewey Williams began learning the shape-note tradition in his childhood. He studied under Judge Jackson, who authored the landmark 1934 hymnbook The Colored Sacred Harp. In 1971, Williams formally organized The Wiregrass Sacred Harp Singers to preserve the music full-time. This unified troupe began touring nationally and leading workshops, which ultimately launched them onto stages at the Smithsonian and Newport folk festivals up until Williams' passing in 1995 when the group disbanded. The African-American Sacred Harp tradition in the Wiregrass region has steeply declined since the start of the 21st century, due to an aging generation of singers, and today it is largely sustained through archival preservation and occasional multi-book singing meetups.

This raw recording, made at the Union Grove Baptist Church, Ozark in mid-April 1993 finds the group singing from B. F. White’s The Sacred Harp (1844), which together with his brother-in-law William Walker’s Southern Harmony (1835) formed the musical backbone of generations of Southern music and Southern musical styles.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑记录了1993年阿拉巴马州奥扎克联合浸信会教堂的现场录音，由Wiregrass Sacred Harp Singers演绎，他们以原始的无伴奏方式演唱B.F. White 1844年《The Sacred Harp》中的赞美诗。领唱Dewey Williams自幼学习形符谱传统，师从《The Colored Sacred Harp》编者Judge Jackson，后于1971年正式组建合唱团，致力于保存非裔美国人形符谱音乐。他们的演唱不依赖乐器伴奏，依靠人声的力量与和声共鸣呈现美国南方黑人教会的宗教传统。这些作品及其演唱风格构成了后来多种南方音乐流派的根基，录音以朴素的现场方式保留了传统歌唱的真实质感。该传统在21世纪初因老一辈歌手凋零而大幅萎缩，如今主要依靠档案保存与偶尔的多声部歌唱聚会延续。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — There is a piggy bank here, and inside it lie precious treasures, such as the debut of one of the great voices: that of Francesco Di Giacomo.The first of the coins stored within is the track titled "R.I.P." (Requiescant In Pace); here, Renato D'Angelo (bass) and Marcello Todaro (guitar) adopt a jazz-infused style, playing with a rhythm and speed that transcend the composition itself, revealing their sheer eagerness to play. While Gianni Nocenzi plays the piano, his brother Vittorio Nocenzi delivers a solo that straddles the line between psychedelia and the Canterbury scene. This very special piggy bank holds coins with two sides, and even three (thanks to that third dimension). That is why the piano takes on a classical tone, mirroring the vocals of Francesco Di Giacomo, a voice destined to be unforgettable from the very first moment you hear it.Passaggio features a harpsichord played by Vittorio Nocenzi; how could one not be captivated by this second "coin", small, yet equally valuable and memorable?Metamorfosi is that elusive coin, kept despite being worn and of dubious origin, whose relief is bold enough to carve out a place in the collection through the sheer force of its hammering piano, like a suite for tails and piano... yet it then mutates, hence the name, into an underground adventure where guitar and organ forge a path through subway tunnels. It is astonishing when the organ takes over the bass lines and the instruments swap roles, all held together by Pier Luigi Calderoni, who constantly shifts rhythms on the drums. When Marcello Todaro enters, he plays with wild, piercing intensity on the electric guitar, while the piano continues with classical scales. This is what should be shown to anyone wanting to experience progressive rock at its peak, music that was once new, wild, and unexpected, and which remains so to this day.Il Giardino Del Mago is the fourth coin... its origin is undetermined, no one knows how it got there, yet it is the oldest and most valuable. It is carved into four parts, with its faces divided. After some choral passages, a hard-rock sound erupts, accompanied by organ, reminiscent of early Deep Purple in its wildness, were it not for the heavily dramatic, operatic, and Mediterranean elements.The second side picks up the pace; the organ, piano, and guitar are just as important as Francesco's tenor voice. In "Chi Ride E Chi Geme," the Emerson, Lake & Palmer-style rush pauses to give way to a section reminiscent of Pink Floyd, evoking Obscured by Clouds, though only until the piano shifts into a classical mode... and everyone joins in singing. Marcello Todaro also features on the third side, with Gianni Nocenzi playing the clarinet as an ancient, distinctly Italian melody blends with progressive rock."Compenetrazione" represents the final side of the coin, where an acoustic guitar heralds the beginning of the end. Such a refined composition is hardly surprising for a 1972 debut, it is a track held in especially high regard. "Traccia" serves as the classical coda they would revisit from time to time, almost a private anthem the group kept for themselves. It is sung by the sextet in a spirit of communion akin to a secret society, a ritualistic bond that seemed to guarantee artistic success.

items._cn_summary: 这张1972年的意大利前卫摇滚首作以存钱罐中的硬币为隐喻，将每首曲目比作不同年代与来源的珍宝。专辑横跨爵士化的即兴段落、古典钢琴语汇与迷幻器乐独奏，吉他与管风琴不断交换主导地位，鼓手则以节奏切换串联全篇。部分段落呈现硬摇滚的猛烈冲击力，混以戏剧性的歌剧化人声与地中海元素；后续曲目则引入羽管键琴、单簧管与原声吉他，融合意大利传统旋律与前卫摇滚结构。人声首秀即展现出极具辨识度的男高音质感。整体编排复杂多变，器乐角色互换的写法展现出强烈的实验意图，但作为意大利前卫摇滚的早期作品，其风格仍以摇滚为骨架，融合元素虽丰富却与当代实验音乐和电子方向有一定距离。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Sweden has a rich history of instrumental progressive rock bands, and the current generation ofartists has some really refreshing things to offer. Stockholm's very own G�sta Berling Saga is oneof these contemporary acts - initially an underground project that slowly gained recognition, thisfour-piece band is now a familiar name in prog circles, and as of 2026 have an impressive sevenstudio albums to their name. 2018 saw the release of 'ET EX' on Sony-owned label Inside Out Music,which would be the band's fifth album. GBS play a fascinating style of instrumental progressive rockthat incorporates elements of symphonic rock, RIO, space rock, and electronica, while the quality ofthe music they create ranges from experimental to dark and expressive - overall, the mixture ofinfluences this band exhibits is quite eclectic. However, 'ET EX' deviates a little from their firstcouple of albums, as it showcases a gloomy synth-laden electronic sound, which has been noted byother reviewers as well.It is almost as if there is a retro synthwave allusion going on, as the listener encounters a vastrange of synthesizer sounds, Mellotrons, and domineering electronic hooks. These are fused reallywell with the rock instruments, by the way, as we hear tons of angular guitar riffs and hypnotic,almost Krautrock-ish rhythms. The atmosphere of this album is undoubtedly darker, but the music isso inventive and tense that one might not necessarily notice the contrasting moods. And so, thesolemn opener 'Veras Tema' leads us to the nearly 8-minute-long song 'The Shortcomings ofEfficiency', where some serpentine guitars forge an upbeat, epic-sounding prog that is quitemesmerizing, too. This is the only track containing vocals, incidentally, as sang by guest musicianMichael Berdan. 'Square 5' is another lengthy composition introducing some wandering electronicsounds, as the music spirals beautifully around the listener, while 'Over and Out' carries a darksynthwave retro feel, which is delightful in a way. 'Capercaillie...' is another peculiar trackreplete with hefty electronics, while the closing track 'Fundament', supposedly the album'scenterpiece, offers a variety of unusual ideas, blending quite naturally G�sta Berling Saga'sexperimental style with the overt 80s influence of 'ET EX'.There is a particularity to this album, meaning that it won't appeal to every single listener, butthe music is excellent all throughout and there is a lot to discover and dive into.
items._cn_summary: 这是瑞典器乐前卫摇滚乐队 Gösta Berling Saga 的第五张专辑。与乐队早期作品相比，本作转向更阴暗的合成器主导路线，融合了大量复古合成器音色、mellotron 与电子钩子，同时保留了棱角分明的吉他 riff 和近似 Krautrock 的催眠律动。整体氛围比以往更为阴沉，但音乐的紧张感与创造性并未因此削弱。开场曲庄严而肃穆，紧接着的长篇曲目在蛇形吉他线条中铺展出史诗般的推进感。专辑贯穿了实验性与明显的八十年代合成器浪潮影响，电子声响与摇滚乐器之间的融合相当自然，乐评人认为这张专辑具有独特气质，不会讨好所有听众，但音乐品质始终在线，值得反复聆听与探索。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "The Blueprint Dives" is the fourth full-length studio album by Norwegian metal act Extol. The albumwas released through Century Media Records in February 2005. It�s the successor to "Synergy" fromAugust 2003. It would be the last release during their original run as Extol disbanding in 2007(they have since reunited). There have been a few lineup changes since "Synergy" as guitaristChrister Espevoll has been replaced by Ole Halvard Sveen and guitarist Ole B�rud has been replacedby a returning Tor Magne Glidje, who had a previous stint with Extol in the 1999-2001 periodalthough back then as the band�s bassist.Stylistically the material on "The Blueprint Dives" is in some ways a continuation of the technical/progressive metal style with Christian themed lyrics of "Synergy". The music features elements ofthrash metal and death metal just as "Synergy" did, but the harder edged metal elements havedecreased since the last album and there�s a lot more clean male singing on "The Blueprint Dives"than on the preceding album (harsh shouting vocals are still a part of the soundscape). Harmonyvocals are now also a part of the soundscape (already heard on album opener "Gloriana") and while"The Blueprint Dives" still features heavy riffs and drumming, it�s a very melodic and accessiblerelease, even touching alternative/heavy progressive rock territories once or twice. I guess this ishow it would sound if late era Death (the band) and late 1990s/early 2000s Enchant met up andcollaborated. Extol definitely have a unique sound which combines a lot of different musicalelements. The more concise songwriting approach of "Synergy" is continued on "The Blueprint Dives" which makesit a nicely accessible listening experience while still being sophisticated and challenging enoughnot to be easy listening. Extol are skilled composers and a very well playing unit too, soeverything on "The Blueprint Dives" is of a high quality. The same can be said about the soundproduction values. "The Blueprint Dives" features a powerful, clear, and detailed sound productionwhich suits the material perfectly. Upon conclusion "The Blueprint Dives" is an interesting stepforward for Extol. They may have lost a few fans because of the more melodic alternative rockapproach of some of the material (a track like "Lost In Dismay" probably won�t please that part ofthe fanbase), but praise must be given to them for the courage to keep evolving and they arguably dowhat they do with great passion and conviction. A 3.5 - 4 star (75%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).
items._genre: progressive metal / extreme metal / technical metal
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是挪威金属乐队Extol的第四张录音室专辑，作为其原活动期最后一张发行物，承接了前作的技术性前卫金属风格，同时明显转向更易听的旋律化方向。编曲中保留了敲击金属与死亡金属的硬朗骨架，但削弱了极端元素的比重，大量引入清声主唱与和声，偶有乐句触及另类与前卫摇滚领域。评论将其比作晚期Death与世纪之交Enchant的融合，表明技术演奏与旋律可听性并存。制作精良，录音清晰有力，乐手技艺成熟，歌曲结构相对紧凑。虽因更柔和的另类摇滚倾向可能流失部分老乐迷，但乐队对风格演化的勇气与热情受到肯定。整体质量稳定，在旋律化前卫金属范畴内属于水准之上的作品。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — (In memory or Roger Keith "Syd" Barrett, 1945-2006, thank you for being my inspiration)Describing the two solo Syd Barrett records, is a difficult task, for a brief period of time between1965, to the early 1970's, Barrett shone bright like the sun in the sky, it is shocking to listen tohis latter works after listening through the whimsical fairy tale like psychedelia of "The piper atthe gates of dawn" and the first Pink Floyd singles, to the dark, gritty and minimalistic sound ofhis solo records (this particular style is way more accentuated on his last three Pink Floyd songs,only one of which was officially released on "A saucerful of secrets", the other 2 on the Earlyyears Pink Floyd box set). These two records illustrate a clear picture of what was going on in hislife during this difficult period for him, they act as autobiographical records if one is to analyzeart trying to get in the author's (this time, musicians) shoes, they're deeply personal and displayan amount of vulnerability seen in very few works, that's where the real impact of "The madcaplaughs" lies...it's the collapse and fall of a legend captured into music, forever to roam and findthose who need it in the right time.The overall aura the music has is somber, mellow, almost detached, yet fully captivating. Thecompositions are quite simple, usually a chord progression consisting on some major chordsintercalated with minor and minor 7 chords, with some chromatic elements and simple strumming on anacoustic guitar, this usually accompanied by Barrett's tired voice, that lazes softly over it alland an occasional synthesiser. The two exceptions that stand out to this rule here are the tracks"Octopus" (which, any musician will be captivated by, because of its strange progression andrhythmic structure) which has an upbeat tone with full band instrumentation and surreal, borderingdadaist lyrics (they remember me of Nicanor Parra in some ways! Although I doubt Barrett had everread Chilean poet Parra at this point I'm his life), and "No good trying", which is incrediblypsychedelic and feels like a mix between colourful yet dark spirals such as those seen in Van Gogh'spaintings and a dark, strong bitter tasting beverage, it also has full band instrumentation and thelyrics are the emotional pivot of the record, as these paint the clearest picture of what Barrettwas trying to express. Despite not being as psychedelic as his previous works, and it all being alittle more simple and amateurish, it's s collection of interesting songs, yes, they're not foreveryone and will not suit the taste of those who seek a complex, detail rich kind of music, butthose who love folk rock and want to get to know Barrett more, will love this kind of music!I really won't get too deep in the production, since it really isn't that special, it suits therecord very well and does a good job at keeping fidelity to the songs, nonetheless I'd like to addthat it was done by none other than his former bandmates and friends David Gilmour and RichardWrigth, who he wouldn't see for some years after the release of his two records, they also acted asstudio musicians (tis but a fun fact that adds even more emotional weight to the overallexperience).The picture the record paints is clear and speaks louder than any biography ever could, since it'scoming right out of our crazy diamond's soul, it serves to humanize the legend and to give acomforting (yet unsettling for those who know it's context) hug to the listener...if you're in foran emotional experience go on, but I warn you that it's not an easy listen and might not be foreveryone, but, if you like Pink Floyd, and want a refreshing record, you'll fall in love with this!Despite knowing he won't ever read this, since he's sadly passed in 2006, thank you very much,Roger, for being my inspiration and giving me moments of comfort amidst hardship, you'll be ineveryone's memories.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑记录了Syd Barrett从辉煌到崩塌的轨迹。整体氛围阴郁、柔和、近乎超脱，却仍具吸引力。作曲简洁，以吉他为基础的和弦进行配合Barrett疲惫的嗓音，偶尔加入合成器。例外之处在于Octopus以其怪异的进行和节奏结构、全乐器编制和接近达达主义的超现实歌词脱颖而出；No Good Trying则色彩斑斓又暗沉，是专辑情感核心。尽管不如早期作品那般迷幻，略显简单和业余，但这些歌曲对民谣摇滚爱好者和想要深入了解Barrett的人而言仍然有趣。从音乐本质来看，作品介于迷幻民谣与艺术摇滚之间，与其主要关注的实验前卫方向有一定距离，但其裸露的个人情感和脆弱表达具有独特的艺术价值。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — It was 1977...and it truly was a whirlwind with the number of scenes happening simultaneously. New York's CBGB club was a breeding ground where bands like Television, who were killing it with Marquee Moon, Blondie, and even the early B-52s, who were as wild as aliens from outer space who had arrived from the 1950s. It was against this backdrop that Talking Heads emerged; having started as a trio in 1975, and initially championed by Lou Reed, who, like John Cale, had seen them at CBGB, the group was ready to record once Jerry Harrison joined on rhythm guitar and keyboards.Between David Byrne's vocals, distinctive right from the start, and Chris Frantz's steel pan, the band had something unique... setting them apart from their peers on the scene, even though they sounded just as raw as everyone else in a live setting. But where they truly made a difference was in their songwriting; the songs had a peculiar construction, all springing from Byrne's mind. "New Feeling" was a prime example of this experimental approach, and the quartet sounded tight and well-oiled.Within the New Wave vehicle, they incorporated rock with punk-like energy, without actually being punk, as well as soul, country, and the backing vocals found in "Tentative Decisions"; meanwhile, traces of Velvet Underground influence can be glimpsed in "Happy Day." "No Compassion" is very interesting; Tina Weymouth's bass work really stands out. There was already a distinctive sound present in Brian Eno's solo work, specifically during his collaborations with Percy Jones, though not in a fusion style, and one can even draw a line connecting it to early R.E.M. in the early 80s."The Book I Read" showcases a powerful voice, one that still had some maturing to do but was already fully present, possessing something of the vocal richness of Adrian Belew. It features a closing coda that could easily fit onto a solo album by Belew, who would later go on to work with the band. A Latin vibe takes over "First Week / Last Week... Carefree," featuring a guest saxophonist (albeit an uncredited one)."Psycho Killer" will forever be the band's classic track, with its driving, funky, provocative opening and Byrne's "psychiatric" vocal delivery; he knew exactly what he was doing, much like Roger Daltrey stuttering his way through "My Generation." The music, phrasing, and lyrics all come together to create an immortal classic and one of many generational anthems. The guitar strumming echoes the cacophonies of The Velvet Underground, the band they grew up listening to."Pulled Up" brings the debut to a close with raw, high-octane energy, a first effort that still had details to refine, yet showcased a style destined to mature beautifully over the next three albums without sacrificing energy or originality. It defied conventions and labels, embracing the freedom found in appearing normal within a world that was (and remains) increasingly anything but.

items._cn_summary: 这张1977年的首张专辑诞生于纽约CBGB俱乐部场景，融合了新浪潮的能量与多元素拼贴。David Byrne的嗓音独树一帜，从开场即展现出实验性的歌曲结构。乐队在新浪潮框架下吸收了朋克的能量、灵魂乐的和声、乡村元素以及拉丁节奏，同时保留Velvet Underground式的吉他质感。Tina Weymouth的贝斯线条在多首曲目中表现突出，Chris Frantz的钢鼓音色为作品增添了辨识度。《Psycho Killer》以放克化的贝斯线与神经质的演唱成为乐队标志，Adrian Belew式的声乐质地和coda段落预示了日后的合作方向。专辑末尾保留了高能的原始粗糙感，但整体已显示出走向成熟的潜力，在不牺牲能量与原创性的前提下实现了风格自觉。

items.body: De/Vision released their synth-pop album “Fairyland?” on 9 August 1996 through Strange Ways Records. The album turns 30 this year. It became the first De/Vision album to enter the German album charts, where it reached number 87 later that month. ‘Fairyland?’, De/Vision’s first chart entry The band recorded the album at The Factory in Belgium in April and May 1996. De/Vision produced and mixed the record together with José Alvarez-Brill, and Tom Meyer mastered it at Master & Servant in Hamburg. Strange Ways Records issued “Fairyland?” on CD, alongside a limited digipak edition of 7,777 copies that came with a 12-page booklet and a band poster. The twelve tracks are “I Regret,” “Dawn,” “Sweet Life,” “Like the Sun,” “Harvester,” “Today’s Life,” “Scars,” “Keep Your Dreams Alive,” “Wages of Sin,” “Bleed Me White,” “Take Me to the Time…” and “Daydreamin’.” The singles “I Regret” and “Sweet Life” accompanied the album in 1996. The album entered the German album charts on 26 August 1996 and peaked at number 87, the band’s first chart placement. Asked in a Q&A on their Apple Music artist page about the most memorable moments of their career, the band pointed straight to this record: “Our first chart success with ‘Fairyland?’ in 1996!” The live album “Fairylive!” followed in 1997. The original 1996 recordings are currently not available on the major streaming services; the album circulates on CD through the secondhand market. About De/Vision De/Vision formed in July 1988 in Bensheim, near Darmstadt, Germany, with Steffen Keth on vocals and Thomas Adam, Markus Ganssert and Stefan Blender on synthesizers. Blender left in 1991. The band self-released the single “Your Hands on My Skin” in 1990 and issued “Boy on the Street” in 1992 through Synthetic Product Records, before the 1993 maxi single “Try to Forget” brought them to Strange Ways Records. The debut album “World Without End” followed in 1994, produced by Axel Henninger, who had previously worked with Camouflage. “Unversed in Love” and “Antiquity” both appeared in 1995, and “Fairyland?” arrived in August 1996 as the band’s first chart album. “Monosex” followed in 1998 through WEA. Markus Ganssert left in 2000, and Keth and Adam have continued as a duo since, now based in Berlin. They founded their own label Popgefahr Records in 2009 and released later albums including “Popgefahr” (2010), “Rockets and Swords” (2012), “13” (2016) and “Citybeats” (2018). Keth also appears in Devision Redux, which went on tour in 2025 with Daniel Myer of Haujobb, while De/Vision themselves joined a 2025 tour with Lakeside X and Empathy Test. The 30th anniversary of “Fairyland?” points back to the album that opened that chart history.

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由音乐考古学家Dominique Cravic与地下漫画家Robert Crumb共同发起的Les Primitifs du futur乐队录制，是其第五张作品。乐队以bal-musette风格为核心，融合拉格泰姆、jug乐队、法国香颂、skiffle等多种难以归类的风格。Cravic以近似Maurice Chevalier的念唱方式演绎27首短曲，配以手风琴、班卓琴、尤克里里、簧风琴、萨克斯、木锯等复古乐器，仿佛从78转唱片库中重新发掘的旧时光碎片。其中包括1925年的幽默老歌《Ukulele Lady》以及向法国抵抗运动传奇女歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的《N'oublie pas Gréco》。评论指出，乐手虽多为七旬老人，却以严肃态度与热情让被遗忘的音乐重新焕发光彩。整体呈现一种跨越时空的拼贴美学，既是对欧洲传统流行音乐的考古式整理，也带有戏谑的收藏家趣味。

items.excerpt: Collective listening events respond to a cultural need, but are at risk of co-option by wellness and lifestyle marketeers, argues Derek Walmsley in The Wire 511 “You’re in the right place!” smiles the man in the smart shirt and trousers at the velvet rope line. items.body: Collective listening events respond to a cultural need, but are at risk of co-option by wellness and lifestyle marketeers, argues Derek Walmsley in The Wire 511 “You’re in the right place!” smiles the man in the smart shirt and trousers at the velvet rope line. Inside a modest door on a touristy street in London’s Soho is a cocktail bar, work space, podcast studio, plus a private cinema which doubles as Polygon Portal, a high spec surround sound listening venue. The occasion is John Coltrane’s centenary, and his Impulse! albums A Love Supreme and John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman are being played for an audience of around 50 people lounging on soft seats and sofas with blindfolds to block out distractions. A ticket costs £25. These kinds of immersive listening experiences are finding an audience. At Polygon Portal, many of their events – which include classic album sessions, curated playlists accompanied by a short history essay, and “wellbeing” events with some kind of meditation or ritual – are sold out. The vibe in the bar beforehand falls somewhere between the taut anticipation of a classy date and the insider chit-chat behind the counter at a record shop. Even if you’ve heard A Love Supreme dozens of times, you pick up something new here. The Polygon set-up takes the original recording and diffuses it across an array of speakers, keeping the stereo separation but allocating frequencies to various cones, tweeters and subwoofers. This particular event does not use surround sound, which might distribute the four instruments of Coltrane’s classic quartet to discrete audio sources around the venue. But the distinction between the players is still impressive, seeming to occupy different areas of the room. The rhythm section of Elvin Jones and Jimmy Garrison in particular comes alive, the vibrations in the air carrying a churning turbulence absent on hi-fi or headphones. Pitchblack Playback is another listening gathering, with events in cities across several continents. A London event includes a free Joni Mitchell eye mask to help you concentrate on Blue (55th anniversary version) and Court And Spark, and there’s even a recorded message from Joni beforehand. There are rules to help everyone get along: no looking at phones, no singing, no latecomers. You commit to listening to each album in its entirety, which strengthens the sense of its structure and logic. Afterwards, my smartphone tells me my heartbeat dropped into a state of deep relaxation over the course of the session. Listening to albums together in public is nothing new. Recorded Music Societies blossomed in the postwar period in the UK, where church halls or libraries hosted gatherings for people to hear records without needing to own costly equipment, with the addition perhaps of an informative talk. London audiophile venue Spiritland opened a decade ago, and in the years since, other listening bars in the city such as Brilliant Corners, Jazu, One Eighty One and the Listening Room at 180 Studios have all offered music heads a place to bond over records. Collective listening experiences address a desire that many feel for a sense of community – seen elsewhere in the renewed interest in crafting, workshops and real life social networks – and for discovering culture outside the circles of apps and algorithms. This demand side now meets a supply side where cinemas and other high street spaces are underused in the post-pandemic era, and London residents often have limited space in their own homes. While it might seem odd to spend a chunk of money to hear music you might easily find online, it scratches a particular itch for some. Immersive listening events often carry a sense of exclusivity. Some sell themselves as part of a digital detox – there are events with guided meditation, yoga, or singing bowls – and while the marketing patter might allude to community and connection, presenting themselves as a sanctuary from the world outside can be read as a kind of snobbery. The idea of getting away from the online world easily blurs into a humblebrag about an enviable alternative lifestyle. The Japanese idea of the jazz kissa – a cafe with a library-like atmosphere in which to appreciate jazz records in particular – gives an extra vibe of distinction to some listening venues. At a time when these venues sometimes struggle for relevance in Japan in the era of the smartphone, their Western iterations have become suddenly chic and fetishised, providing an aspirational oasis of Eastern calm with ticket prices to match. This kind of branding plays out on Instagram and other social media channels, despite the promise that listening venues constitute a break from online life. Polygon Portal have ambitious ideas. They plan to parlay the attraction of spatial audio into nightclub, restaurant and even gym destinations. These would no doubt all be beautiful experiences, but the more chic the marketing pitch gets, the more alienating some may find it. At present, listening events often look backwards. Many of the albums featured in immersive listening sessions crop up as they hit an anniversary, or emerge in a glossy new reissue. While that helps to fill venues with committed fans, it also creates a somewhat predictable merry-go-round of familiar classics. As with any artistic canon, unless it’s refreshed, stretched and tested, it feels destined to become stale. For immersive sound experiences to fulfil their creative potential, they need to be open and accessible, firstly to different audiences, and also to relationships with other bodies. A varied approach to curation would ensure that legacy rock reissues don’t dominate the music that’s presented. And reaching out to other organisations might make them less exclusive, more connected to culture’s grassroots, and give them a broader social mission. There’s a future in which DIY organisations, festivals, collectives, multi-disciplinary bodies and other cultural incubators use collective listening to forge stronger connections between audiences and music. If listeners are revisiting King Crimson or Joni Mitchell, why not the music of Terry Riley, Pharoah Sanders, Julius Eastman, Maryanne Amacher, Pauline Oliveros, Alvin Lucier, or any number of avant garde or experimental touchstones? By exploring music found off the beaten track, these kinds of events could serve to change and refresh canons, and not just replicate them. This essay appears in The Wire 511. Wire subscribers can also read it in our online magazine library.

items.body: Soft Vein, the California-based electronic project of Justin Chamberlain, will release his third studio album, “All We’ve Known of Heaven,” on September 4, 2026 through Artoffact Records. The album arrives on a limited dark blue vinyl LP and on CD in a jewel box with booklet, alongside digital and streaming formats. Soft Vein bring a sound that mixes synthpop and sophisti-pop, with lush synthesizers, sparkling guitars and melodic vocals set against themes of nostalgia, romance, homesickness, personal growth and change. “All We’ve Known of Heaven” is co-produced by Soft Vein and Andrea Mantione of Nuovo Testamento, mixed by Chamberlain himself, and mastered by Jason Corbett of ACTORS at Jacknife Sound in Vancouver. Saxophonist Rachel Mazer guests on two tracks. The eight-track album runs “Another Summer,” “Chekhov,” “Learning to Talk,” “Proof of Life,” “White Towers (White Shores),” “Forgetting You,” “Living in Liminal Spaces” and the title track, “All We’ve Known of Heaven.” All We’ve Known of Heaven by Soft Vein Soft Vein’s title-track video for ‘All We’ve Known of Heaven’ Chamberlain shared an official video for “All We’ve Known of Heaven,” directed by Sydney Mills with cinematography by Cameron Dunbar. About Soft Vein Soft Vein is the solo electronic project of Los Angeles-based songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Justin Chamberlain. The project broke into the Los Angeles darkwave scene with a pair of early singles before signing to Artoffact Records and releasing its debut album, “Pressed in Glass,” in October 2023. Chamberlain followed with the second album, “Through Blinds,” in January 2025 and the EP “From Another Room” in June 2025, alongside the singles “Chekhov” and “All We’ve Known of Heaven” earlier in 2026. “All We’ve Known of Heaven,” due September 4, 2026, marks Soft Vein’s third full-length and was recorded during winter 2025/2026 at Seahorse Sound in Los Angeles and Jacknife Sound in Vancouver.

Megamantra by Black Magnet About Black Magnet Black Magnet started as the solo project of Midwestern US musician James Hammontree and has since expanded into a trio with the addition of Jared Branson and Ryne Bratcher, who also play with All Your Sisters, Destroyer Destroyer and Greg Puciato. The band released two albums through 20 Buck Spin before signing with Federal Prisoner, the label co-founded by artist Jesse Draxler and Greg Puciato of The Dillinger Escape Plan and Better Lovers, for its third album, “Megamantra,” released July 25, 2025. “Megamantra” was recorded at Earth Analogue Studio, engineered and mixed by Sanford Parker, mastered by Vlado Meller, and features additional synthesizers and background vocals by Eric Gorman. Black Magnet has toured as support for 3Teeth, Code Orange and Author & Punisher, and now returns to the road for its first European tour, which brings the band to Brussels for the first time on September 8, 2026.

items.body:
2026 Re-press of "Spaghetti Circus" by Still Going on DFA Records.

"Still Going arrived on the scene with “Still Going Theme,” a seductive layering of deep, creeping bass, swelling synths and tinkling pianos atop a disco pulse. Along with its hypnotic flipside, “On and On,” the single captivated listeners with its anthemic energy and quickly became a dance floor staple. With the release of “Spaghetti Circus,” Olivier “Liv” Spencer and Eric “Dunks” Duncan build on their reputation for creating compelling dance music for compulsive listening.

This record is two years in the making, time the duo spent churning out a steady stream of remixes for an impressive roster of musicians, including The Presets, !!!, Crazy P, Force of Nature, Doves and Low Motion Disco. They've also been busy with their respective DJ projects – Dunks with the infamous duo Rub-N-Tug and Liv as one half of dance favorites House of House. On the heels of these numerous endeavors, Still Going have managed to return with a stellar new release.

“Spaghetti Circus,” the title track, pairs rubbery bass with trance-inducing waves of swooning, orchestral keys and dramatic piano. The B-Side, “Untitled Love,” changes the mood, settling comfortably into a space-ious, swaggering mid-tempo groove. Set against these lush backdrops are vocals from Reggie Watts, a singer whose performances both live and on record have established him as an immense talent. Watt’s urgent, rough-hewn voice serves to propel the driving rhythm of “Spaghetti Circus,” while on “Untitled Love,” his soulfully smooth vocals anchor the track’s languid pace.

Other featured performances on this long-awaited 12” are sure to generate even more enthusiasm for its release. Andrew Raposo, formerly of Hercules & Love Affair and now of Jessica 6, Midnight Magic and Tippy Toes, plays bass on both songs. Jason Rabe of Los Angeles-based band The VLA contributes lead guitar to “Spaghetti Circus” And Tim Lee, founder of noted electronic label Tummy Touch Records, plays the Rhodes on “Untitled Love.” "
items._cn_summary: Still Going 是 DFA Records 旗下双人组合，由 Liv Spencer 与 Eric Duncan 组成，时隔两年推出这张十二寸单曲唱片。标题曲《Spaghetti Circus》以弹性的贝斯线为基底，叠加迷幻合成器浪潮、管弦乐色彩键盘与戏剧化钢琴，营造出催眠式的迪斯科律动。b 面《Untitled Love》转向中速太空放克质感。Reggie Watts 以粗粝紧迫的人声驱动前曲，又以灵魂化平滑的演绎锚定后曲的慵懒节奏。贝斯手 Andrew Raposo、吉他手 Jason Rabe 与键盘手 Tim Lee 等客座乐手丰富了层次。整体制作精致，融合了迪斯科、合成器放克与俱乐部舞曲元素，属于 DFA 招牌式的派对音乐路线。

items.body:
Big room fuel by Tom & Ed Russell’s Overmono, condensing and refining the energy of their ‘Pure Devotion’ megadome events into Pavlovian cues for obedient ravers. OK no bush-beating, it’s torrid stuff that epitomises the schism of music for clubs, dancing, vs corporate-sponsored stages, PR, playlists...

“Sharing a name with the beloved series of live events they launched in 2024, Pure Devotion is Overmono’s most ambitious project to date. It’s the sound of beautiful imperfections, machine malfunctions and happy accidents, harnessed by the unflinching confidence that Overmono - aka brothers Tom and Ed Russell - have gained through years at the vanguard of underground electronic music, and subsequent breakthrough as one of the defining dance music acts of the decade.

Across the 11 tracks, Overmono have pushed their recording process into bold new territories, adopting experimental production techniques that involve synthesisers from the 70s and 80s, an antiquated train announcement speaker, and literally baking a crash cymbal in the oven. There’s a powerful sense of intention and physicality embedded in every choice, which extends to the emotive vocal features from revered British poet John Joseph Holt, close collaborator Kindora, and Paul Institute’s Ruthven It’s an album that chooses emotion over desensitisation. Craft over efficiency. It's a labour of love. Pure Devotion.

What started as a radical reimagining of Overmono’s live show in 2024 evolved into a phenomenon - from headlining Glastonbury’s West Holts to selling out London’s Alexandra Palace and curating Manchester’s Warehouse Project. As Pure Devotion grew onstage in front of tens of thousands of people, its core ideas deepened and crystallised via isolated writing and recordings retreats to Spain and Iceland with nothing but two synths and an FX unit, channeling the momentum into the most life-affirming and groundbreaking music of their career.”

items.body:
Classy haul of dancehall and street soul-adjacent Zouk from the Caribbean isles, cooked up by Disques Debs, Radio Nova, and Tropical Discoteq programer Émile Omar. Check for the orchestral dates and raggo Créole flow of ‘Mwen inmin’ by Metal Sound; the syrupy sway of Claudy Siar and O’Taïm gems; the low-slung rap of X’Taz.

“Back to the golden nights of zouk clubs, where hip-hop, kompa, zouk and Caribbean grooves ruled the dance-floor. This selection documents a pivotal moment : a time when zouk was still not a fixed genre, but more a place, an atmosphere, somewhere people went to dance. It captures the spirit of an era: its creative effervescence, musical freedom, and the diversity of artists who shaped it. The very concept of “Kaz A Zouk” perfectly encapsulates this idea: a space where all styles could meet.”

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由法国海外推广人Émile Omar策划，汇编了1987至1998年间加勒比海群岛的舞厅音乐与街头灵魂乐录音，涵盖zouk、kompa、克里奥尔说唱与ragga等多种风格，源于Disques Debs等厂牌档案。乐评指出选辑聚焦于zouk尚未固化为固定类型的历史阶段，强调其作为舞蹈场所与氛围的原始含义，捕捉了多元艺术家汇聚的音乐自由与创作活力。具体曲目亮点包括Metal Sound的管弦编曲与克里奥尔说唱流、Claudy Siar与O'Taïm的柔缓律动、以及X'Taz的低沉说唱。该合辑虽展现加勒比地区音乐文化的丰富性与跨风格交融，但整体定位于舞蹈导向的商业舞厅流行，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、爵士及电子领域距离较远，缺乏显著的创新声音设计或前卫元素。
